        "cna": {
          "title": "Cacti: Command Injection via escape_command() no-op in RRDtool execution",
          "problemTypes": [
            {
              "descriptions": [
                {
                  "cweId": "CWE-78",
                  "lang": "en",
                  "description": "CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')",
                  "type": "CWE"
                }
              ]
            },
            {
              "descriptions": [
                {
                  "cweId": "CWE-88",
                  "lang": "en",
                  "description": "CWE-88: Improper Neutralization of Argument Delimiters in a Command ('Argument Injection')",
                  "type": "CWE"
                }
              ]
            }
          ],
          "metrics": [
            {
              "cvssV4_0": {
                "attackVector": "NETWORK",
                "attackComplexity": "LOW",

                "baseScore": 8.6,
                "baseSeverity": "HIGH",
                "vectorString": "CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:H/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:L/SI:L/SA:L",
                "version": "4.0"
              }
            }
          ],
          "references": [
            {
              "name": "https://github.com/Cacti/cacti/security/advisories/GHSA-xq98-376r-hv9j",

                "x_refsource_CONFIRM"
              ],
              "url": "https://github.com/Cacti/cacti/security/advisories/GHSA-xq98-376r-hv9j"
            },
            {
              "name": "https://github.com/Cacti/cacti/commit/4c09efaebf3a9faec66969d0b5c4aceaf397f37f",
              "tags": [
                "x_refsource_MISC"
              ],
              "url": "https://github.com/Cacti/cacti/commit/4c09efaebf3a9faec66969d0b5c4aceaf397f37f"
            }
          ],
          "affected": [
            {
              "vendor": "Cacti",
              "product": "cacti",
              "versions": [
                {
                  "version": "< 1.2.31",
                  "status": "affected"
                }
              ]
            }
          ],
          "providerMetadata": {
            "orgId": "a0819718-46f1-4df5-94e2-005712e83aaa",
            "shortName": "GitHub_M",
            "dateUpdated": "2026-06-24T23:26:40.623Z"
          },
          "descriptions": [
            {
              "lang": "en",
              "value": "Cacti is an open source performance and fault management framework. Versions 1.2.30 and prior are vulnerable to Command Injection due to lack of sanitization in the escape_command() function. The escape_command() function at lib/rrd.php is a no-op: it returns $command unchanged. The command line built by rrdtool_function_graph() is passed through this function and then to shell_exec($full_commandline). The risk is in __rrd_execute() where text_format values from graph templates (which may contain host variable substitutions) reach shell_exec without adequate escaping. This issue has been addressed in version 1.2.31."
            }
          ],
          "source": {
            "advisory": "GHSA-xq98-376r-hv9j",
            "discovery": "UNKNOWN"
          },
          "x_gcve": [
            {
              "recordType": "advisory",
              "vulnId": "cve-2026-40079"
            }
          ]
        }
      },

          "title": "Quest NetVault Backup viewclient Cross-Site Scripting Authentication Bypass Vulnerability",
          "descriptions": [
            {
              "lang": "en",
              "value": "Quest NetVault Backup viewclient Cross-Site Scripting Authentication Bypass Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to bypass authentication on affected installations of Quest NetVault Backup. User interaction is required to exploit this vulnerability in that the target must visit a malicious page or open a malicious file.\n\nThe specific flaw exists within the viewclient webpage. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of user-supplied data, which can lead to the injection of an arbitrary script. An attacker can leverage this in conjunction with other vulnerabilities to execute arbitrary code in the context of SYSTEM. Was ZDI-CAN-28202."
            }
          ],

              "value": "Quest NetVault Backup NVBULogDaemon Command Injection Remote Code Execution Vulnerability.             "shortName": "zdi",
            "dateUpdated": "2026-06-24T23:15:05.276Z"
          },
          "title": "Quest NetVault Backup NVBUDashboard SQL Injection Remote Code Execution Vulnerability",
          "descriptions": [
            {
              "lang": "en",
              "value": "Quest NetVault Backup NVBUDashboard SQL Injection Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of Quest NetVault Backup. Although authentication is required to exploit this vulnerability, the existing authentication mechanism can be bypassed.\n\nThe specific flaw exists within the processing of NVBUDashboard JSON-RPC messages. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of a user-supplied string before using it to construct SQL queries. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute code in the context of NETWORK SERVICE. Was ZDI-CAN-27626."
            }
          ],
          "affected": [
            {
              "vendor": "Quest",
              "product": "NetVault Backup",
              "versions": [

            "dateUpdated": "2026-06-24T23:13:55.522Z"
          },
          "title": "Quest NetVault Backup addclient3 Cross-Site Scripting Authentication Bypass Vulnerability",
          "descriptions": [
            {
              "lang": "en",
              "value": "Quest NetVault Backup addclient3 Cross-Site Scripting Authentication Bypass Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to bypass authentication on affected installations of Quest NetVault Backup. User interaction is required to exploit this vulnerability in that the target must visit a malicious page or open a malicious file.\n\nThe specific flaw exists within the addclient3 webpage. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of user-supplied data, which can lead to the injection of an arbitrary script. An attacker can leverage this in conjunction with other vulnerabilities to execute arbitrary code in the context of SYSTEM. Was ZDI-CAN-27666."
            }
          ],
          "affected": [
            {
              "vendor": "Quest",
              "product": "NetVault Backup",

          },
          "title": "Quest NetVault Backup NVBUDashboard SQL Injection Remote Code Execution Vulnerability",
          "descriptions": [
            {
              "lang": "en",
              "value": "Quest NetVault Backup NVBUDashboard SQL Injection Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of Quest NetVault Backup. Although authentication is required to exploit this vulnerability, the existing authentication mechanism can be bypassed.\n\nThe specific flaw exists within the processing of NVBUDashboard JSON-RPC messages. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of a user-supplied string before using it to construct SQL queries. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute code in the context of NETWORK SERVICE. Was ZDI-CAN-27809."
            }
          ],
          "affected": [
            {

              "product": "NetVault Backup",

        "cveId": "CVE-2026-39948",
        "assignerOrgId": "a0819718-46f1-4df5-94e2-005712e83aaa",
        "state": "PUBLISHED",
        "assignerShortName": "GitHub_M",
        "dateReserved": "2026-04-07T22:40:33.821Z",
        "datePublished": "2026-06-24T23:06:39.057Z",
        "dateUpdated": "2026-06-24T23:06:39.057Z"
      },
      "containers": {
        "cna": {
          "title": "Cacti has SQL Injection via rfilter parameter in RLIKE clauses",
          "problemTypes": [
            {
              "descriptions": [
                {
                  "cweId": "CWE-89",
                  "lang": "en",
                  "description": "CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')",
                  "type": "CWE"
                }
              ]
            }
          ],
          "metrics": [
            {
              "cvssV4_0": {
                "attackVector": "NETWORK",
                "attackComplexity": "LOW",
                "attackRequirements": "NONE",
                "privilegesRequired": "NONE",
                "userInteraction": "NONE",
                "vulnConfidentialityImpact": "HIGH",
                "vulnIntegrityImpact": "HIGH",
                "vulnAvailabilityImpact": "NONE",
                "subConfidentialityImpact": "NONE",
                "subIntegrityImpact": "NONE",
                "subAvailabilityImpact": "NONE",
                "baseScore": 9.3,
                "baseSeverity": "CRITICAL",
                "vectorString": "CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N",
                "version": "4.0"
              }
            }
          ],
          "references": [
            {
              "name": "https://github.com/Cacti/cacti/security/advisories/GHSA-9jqv-4cpm-vm2c",
              "tags": [
                "x_refsource_CONFIRM"
              ],
              "url": "https://github.com/Cacti/cacti/security/advisories/GHSA-9jqv-4cpm-vm2c"
            },
            {
              "name": "https://github.com/Cacti/cacti/commit/136ae6ef0715e77bca69c0eb60781f5e17df0795",
              "tags": [
                "x_refsource_MISC"
              ],
              "url": "https://github.com/Cacti/cacti/commit/136ae6ef0715e77bca69c0eb60781f5e17df0795"
            }
          ],
          "affected": [
            {
              "vendor": "Cacti",
              "product": "cacti",
              "versions": [
                {
                  "version": "< 1.2.31",
                  "status": "affected"
                }
              ]
            }
          ],
          "providerMetadata": {
            "orgId": "a0819718-46f1-4df5-94e2-005712e83aaa",
            "shortName": "GitHub_M",
            "dateUpdated": "2026-06-24T23:06:39.057Z"
          },
          "descriptions": [
            {
              "lang": "en",
              "value": "Cacti is an open source performance and fault management framework. In versions 1.2.30 and prior, the rfilter request parameter is retrieved via the raw accessor grv() (rather than gfrv() with FILTER_VALIDATE_IS_REGEX validation) and concatenated directly into RLIKE SQL clauses in lib/html_graph.php and lib/html_tree.php, which are reachable pre-authentication through graph_view.php on installations with guest graph viewing enabled. Because the unbalanced-quote payload bypasses the regex validation that would otherwise reject it, an unauthenticated attacker can inject arbitrary SQL to compromise the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the database. This advisory is similar to GHSA-69gg-mjfm-jjpc. This issue has been fixed in version 1.2.31."
            }
          ],
          "source": {
            "advisory": "GHSA-9jqv-4cpm-vm2c",
            "discovery": "UNKNOWN"
          },
          "x_gcve": [
            {
              "recordType": "advisory",
              "vulnId": "cve-2026-39948"
            }
          ]
        }
      },
      "feed_id": "cve",
      "fetched_at": "2026-06-24T19:17:41.977330"
    },

      "summary": "Malicious code in syco1 (npm)",
      "details": "\n---\n_-= Per source details. Do not edit below this line.=-_\n\n## Source: amazon-inspector (e43be65a0930b121cf4d610c70b2d07165e4d335dece4344590b471d078fa5b5)\nPackage self-describes as a 'System binary configuration tool' but ships a covert screen and clipboard surveillance overlay. pointer.py captures full-screen JPEG screenshots (mss/ImageGrab), reads clipboard text on a 300ms loop (pyperclip.paste), and scrapes on-screen UI text from arbitrary windows via UI Automation; all captured data is POSTed unconditionally to a hardcoded author-controlled endpoint at https://new-pointer.vercel.app/api (pointer.py:33 VERCEL_API_URL). The destination is not configurable. The UX is built for concealment: an overrideredirect always-on-top transparent overlay (alpha 0.75, transparent-white) and hidden hotkeys including ctrl+q panic_exit (os._exit), esc stealth_hide, and 1+` stealth_show. The npm wrapper (index.js startApp) additionally performs a silent 'ghost install' of Python 3.12.3 from python.org into %TEMP% via curl, executed with /quiet InstallAllUsers=0 PrependPath=1 and comments explicitly describing the goal as 'No UI, No Admin Popup' \u2014 bootstrapping the Python runtime required by pointer.py without user consent. Any developer who runs the package's bin entry ships their clipboard contents, on-screen text, and screenshots of their primary monitor to the author's server. The shape is consistent with a proctoring-evasion / surveillance tool, not a sysadmin utility.\n",

    {

      "id": "MAL-2026-5616",
      "summary": "Malicious code in sysbu (npm)",
      "details": "\n---\n_-= Per source details. Do not edit below this line.=-_\n\n## Source: amazon-inspector (c7d7e10321db9abd5e77b0f656d5fac237968ecd79c0ce409b58ee555fb5b236)\nDespite advertising itself as a 'System binary configuration tool', sysbu's index.js unconditionally invokes startApp() on require/CLI execution. If Python is not present, it silently installs Python 3.12 \u2014 first via `winget install Python.Python.3.12`, falling back to downloading https://www.python.org/ftp/python/3.12.3/python-3.12.3-amd64.exe to %TEMP% and running it with `/quiet InstallAllUsers=0 PrependPath=1`. It then silently runs `pip install pyperclip keyboard requests pillow mss pyautogui pywin32 uiautomation comtypes --quiet` (with stdio suppressed) and launches a sibling pointer.py. pointer.py creates a hidden topmost transparent Tk overlay, polls `pyperclip.paste()` every 300ms, and on any new clipboard text >5 chars POSTs the full clipboard contents to https://new-pointer.vercel.app/api. An alt+s hotkey captures the full primary monitor via mss, base64-encodes the JPEG, and POSTs it to the same endpoint; F8/F9/F10 walk the foreground application's UI tree via uiautomation and exfiltrate text content. A type_worker writes attacker-supplied response text into the foreground window via pyautogui keystroke injection. ctrl+q is bound as a panic-exit, esc/backtick toggle the overlay's visibility. The advertised purpose, name, and keywords (system/binary/util/config) are a cover story for a clipboard/screen exfiltration and remote-keystroke-injection payload \u2014 likely an interview-cheating tool given the mode names ('aptitude','dsa','fullstack','aws','ocr'). Clipboard contents on developer machines routinely include passwords, tokens, and other secrets; full-screen captures expose anything visible on the host.\n",

      "details": "\n---\n_-= Per source details. Do not edit below this line.=-_\n\n## Source: amazon-inspector (2b9246e768a775d54485e7208d0ed4fc575af09bc78c3fde95c5cb24ebc2350d)\nPackage advertises itself as a 'System binary configuration tool' but ships pointer.py (spawned by index.js) which hardcodes VERCEL_API_URL='https://iq-overlay-pointer.vercel.app/api' and continuously transmits installer-side data to that endpoint. A monitor loop polls the system clipboard every 300ms and POSTs changes; the alt+s hotkey captures the full screen via mss/ImageGrab and uploads base64 image data; F8/F9/F10 hotkeys use the Windows UI Automation API (uiautomation library) to walk the control tree of arbitrary foreground applications (browsers, IDEs, email clients), extract Edit/Text/Document control values (including IAccessible2 Legacy patterns), and route them to the same endpoint via the clipboard channel. To enable this on machines without Python, index.js silently installs a Python runtime \u2014 first attempting winget --silent, then falling back to downloading python-3.12.3-amd64.exe from python.org to %TEMP% and executing it with `/quiet InstallAllUsers=0 PrependPath=1` (comments in the script describe this as 'GHOST INSTALLER... No UI, No Admin Popup'). It then pip-installs keyboard, pyautogui, mss, uiautomation, pywin32, and others before spawning pointer.py. pointer.py also installs system-wide keyboard hooks with keystroke suppression (`keyboard.on_press(..., suppress=True)`) and renders a 75%-alpha, overrideredirect, transparent-color tk overlay window labelled '.' \u2014 a stealth UI consistent with a covert surveillance/interview-cheating overlay rather than the advertised binary configuration utility. None of this behavior is disclosed in the package metadata.\n",

      "summary": "Malicious code in syspo (npm)",
      "details": "\n---\n_-= Per source details. Do not edit below this line.=-_\n\n## Source: amazon-inspector (6f89c590b7c90182cb86bc3e45f71f2357003f4359b6e94818fc996951762f5c)\nThe package is published as a 'System binary configuration tool' but its actual behavior is a covert clipboard/screen-capture overlay. On invocation (npx/bin entry), index.js spawns pointer.py, which installs a global clipboard monitor and an Alt+S full-screen screenshot hotkey; clipboard text and base64-encoded screenshots are POSTed to the hardcoded endpoint https://iq-overlay-pointer.vercel.app/api with no configuration option for the destination and no user disclosure. To bootstrap that payload, index.js silently downloads python-3.12.3-amd64.exe from python.org into TEMP and runs it with `/quiet InstallAllUsers=0 PrependPath=1`, then runs `pip install` for keyboard, pyautogui, mss, pywin32, and uiautomation \u2014 a full language runtime and input/screen-capture toolchain installed without any prompt. pointer.py also registers system-wide keyboard hooks (ctrl+c/v, alt+s, f8/f9/f10, alt+m, alt+1..5, ctrl+q panic-exit) and an always-on-top transparent Tk overlay (`-topmost`, `overrideredirect`), and types attacker-controlled responses back via pyautogui. The package.json metadata (description 'System binary configuration tool', keywords system/binary/util/config, author 'SysDev') is a cover story unrelated to the shipped functionality.\n",

      "summary": "Malicious code in sypoi1 (npm)",
      "details": "\n---\n_-= Per source details. Do not edit below this line.=-_\n\n## Source: amazon-inspector (b22a9450e70ba1095097d2779ad6da01c111c37e940d890fbfc21d1aeb6a0f11)\nOn require, index.js silently bootstraps a full Python runtime on the installer's machine \u2014 first via `winget install -e --id Python.Python.3.12 --silent`, falling back to downloading `python-3.12.3-amd64.exe` from python.org and executing it with `/quiet InstallAllUsers=0 PrependPath=1` \u2014 then silently `pip install`s pyautogui, keyboard, mss, pillow, pyperclip, and uiautomation. It then spawns pointer.py, which installs system-wide hotkeys (Ctrl+C, Alt+S, F8/F9/F10, Alt+M, Ctrl+Q), creates a topmost transparent always-on-top Tk window using `overrideredirect(True)` to hide from the user, continuously monitors clipboard contents, and on hotkeys captures full-monitor screenshots and on-screen text via UI Automation. Captured clipboard text and base64-encoded screenshots are POSTed to a hardcoded destination at `https://iq-overlay-pointer.vercel.app/api`. The agent also exposes a `mash_callback` mode that hooks `keyboard.on_press` with `suppress=True` and substitutes attacker-supplied characters via `pyautogui.write(char)`, injecting keystrokes into whatever window is focused. The package's declared purpose \u2014 \"System binary configuration tool\" by author \"SysDev\" with keywords system/binary/util/config \u2014 does not match any of this behavior; the metadata is a cover story for a screen/clipboard surveillance and remote-keystroke-injection agent.\n",

        "cna": {

            "orgId": "8254265b-2729-46b6-b9e3-3dfca2d5bfca",

            "dateUpdated": "2026-06-24T21:59:01.795Z"
          },
          "descriptions": [
            {
              "lang": "en",
              "value": "GPAC Multimedia Open Source Project GPAC Project/MP4Box 2.5-DEV-rev1593-gfe88c3545-master is affected by: Buffer Overflow. The impact is: cause a denial of service (local). The component is: filter_core/filter_pid.c (L:574-580): function gf_filter_pid_inst_swap_delete_task() improperly accesses freed objects during PID instance swap/delete cleanup, leading to heap use-after-free. The attack vector is: Local (AV:L): a local, authenticated user who processes a specially crafted MPEG-2 TS/MP4 file with MP4Box can trigger the bug during filter teardown (PID instance swap/delete), causing a crash. \u00b6\u00b6 In GPAC s MP4Box, gf_filter_pid_inst_swap_delete_task() in filter_core/filter_pid.c may dereference objects after they have been freed when cleaning up PID instances after a swap/delete operation. Crafted inputs (e.g., malformed MPEG-2 TS) can trigger a heap use-after-free and crash; exploitation may be possible."
            }
          ],
          "affected": [

            "description": "SVRLOT\n\nThe National Weather Service in Chicago has issued a\n\n* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...\nSouth central Kendall County in northeastern Illinois...\nNorthern Grundy County in northeastern Illinois...\n\n* Until 815 PM CDT.\n\n* At 718 PM CDT, a severe thunderstorm was located near Morris,\nmoving southeast at 20 mph.\n\nHAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.\n\nSOURCE...Radar indicated.\n\nIMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected.             "description": "At 618 PM MDT, a confirmed tornado was located 5 miles north of\nFleming, or 19 miles northeast of Sterling, moving southeast at 20\nmph.\n\nHAZARD...Damaging tornado and baseball size hail.\n\nSOURCE...Law enforcement confirmed tornado.\n\nIMPACT...Flying debris will be dangerous to those caught without\nshelter.             "description": "* WHAT...Dense fog will reduce visibility to 1/4 NM or less.\n\n* WHERE...Two Harbors to Duluth MN and Duluth MN to Port Wing WI.\n\n* WHEN...Until 10 AM CDT Thursday.\n\n* IMPACTS...Low visibility will make navigation difficult.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The poorest visibility is expected within 5\nNM of the Twin Ports.             "headline": "Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued June 24 at 6:16PM MDT until June 24 at 7:00PM MDT by NWS North Platte NE",
            "description": "At 615 PM MDT, a severe thunderstorm was located over Chappell,\nmoving east northeast at 40 mph.\n\nHAZARD...Ping pong ball size hail and 60 mph wind gusts.\n\nSOURCE...Radar indicated.\n\nIMPACT...People and animals outdoors will be injured. Expect hail\ndamage to roofs, siding, windows, and vehicles. Expect wind\ndamage to roofs, siding, and trees.\n\nLocations impacted include...\nChappell, Big Springs, Barton, Goldeneye State Wildlife Management\nArea, Mount Vernon, and Intersection of Highway 27 and 9 Mile Road.\n\nThis includes Interstate 80 in Nebraska between mile markers 78 and\n101, and near mile marker 108.",
            "instruction": "For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a\nbuilding.\n\nTo report severe weather contact your nearest law enforcement agency.\nThey will send your report to the National Weather Service office in\nNorth Platte.\n\nTorrential rainfall is occurring with this storm, and may lead to\nflash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded roadways.",
            "response": "Shelter",

            "description": "TORBOU\n\nThe National Weather Service in Denver has issued a\n\n* Tornado Warning for...\nEast Central Logan County in northeastern Colorado...\n\n* Until 645 PM MDT.\n\n* At 613 PM MDT, a confirmed tornado was located 5 miles northwest of\nFleming, or 19 miles northeast of Sterling, moving southeast at 15\nmph.\n\nHAZARD...Damaging tornado and baseball size hail.\n\nSOURCE...Law enforcement confirmed tornado.\n\nIMPACT...Flying debris will be dangerous to those caught without\nshelter. Mobile homes will be damaged or destroyed. Damage\nto roofs, windows and vehicles will occur. Tree damage is\nlikely.\n\n* Locations impacted include...\nFleming and Crook.",
            "instruction": "Move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a well-built building\naway from windows. If you are outdoors, in a mobile home, or in a\nvehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter and protect yourself\nfrom flying debris.",

            "senderName": "NWS Milwaukee/Sullivan WI",
            "headline": "Tornado Warning issued June 24 at 7:12PM CDT until June 24 at 7:30PM CDT by NWS Milwaukee/Sullivan WI",
            "description": "At 712 PM CDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing a tornado\nwas located over Mayville, moving southeast at 25 mph.\n\nHAZARD...Tornado and quarter size hail.\n\nSOURCE...Radar indicated rotation.\n\nIMPACT...Flying debris will be dangerous to those caught without\nshelter. Mobile homes will be damaged or destroyed. Damage\nto roofs, windows, and vehicles will occur.  Tree damage is\nlikely.\n\nThis dangerous storm will be near...\nMayville and Theresa around 720 PM CDT.\n\nOther locations impacted by this tornadic thunderstorm include\nKekoskee.",
            "instruction": "TAKE COVER NOW! Move to a basement or an interior room on the lowest\nfloor of a sturdy building. Avoid windows. If you are outdoors, in a\nmobile home, or in a vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter\nand protect yourself from flying debris.",
            "response": "Shelter",
            "note": null,

            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Kansas City/Pleasant Hill MO",
            "headline": "Flood Watch issued June 24 at 7:12PM CDT until June 26 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Kansas City/Pleasant Hill MO",
            "description": "* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be\npossible.\n\n* WHERE...Portions of Kansas, including the following areas, Johnson\nKS, Leavenworth, Linn KS, Miami and Wyandotte and Missouri,\nincluding the following areas, Bates, Cass, Clay, Cooper, Henry,\nHoward, Jackson, Johnson MO, Lafayette, Pettis, Platte and Saline.\n\n* WHEN...From Thursday afternoon through Friday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,\ncreeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- A very moist airmass in place will bring the potential for high\nrainfall rates and flooding with any thunderstorms.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood\nWarnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared\nto take action should flooding develop.",
            "response": "Prepare",
            "note": null,

            "senderName": "NWS Pocatello ID",
            "headline": "Special Weather Statement issued June 24 at 6:08PM MDT by NWS Pocatello ID",
            "description": "At 607 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm near\nOneida Narrows Reservoir, or 17 miles east of Swanlake, moving\nnortheast at 25 mph.\n\nHAZARD...Wind gusts in excess of 35 mph and half inch hail.\n\nSOURCE...Radar indicated.\n\nIMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around\nunsecured objects. Minor hail damage to outdoor objects is\npossible.\n\nLocations impacted include...\nMontpelier, Georgetown, Oneida Narrows Reservoir, Thatcher, Bern,\nGeorgetown Summit, Emmigrant Summit, Liberty, Bennington, and Clear\nCreek Ranger Station.",
            "instruction": "If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.\n\nFrequent cloud to ground lightning is occurring with this storm.\nLightning can strike 10 miles away from a thunderstorm. Seek a safe\nshelter inside a building or vehicle.",
            "response": "Execute",
            "note": null,

            "description": "At 608 PM MDT, a severe thunderstorm was located 16 miles east of\nBottomless Lakes State Park, or 26 miles east of Roswell, moving\nnorth at 10 mph.\n\nHAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.\n\nSOURCE...Radar indicated.\n\nIMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected.             "description": "SVRCYS\n\nThe National Weather Service in Cheyenne has issued a\n\n* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...\nSouthern Goshen County in southeastern Wyoming...\n\n* Until 645 PM MDT.\n\n* At 606 PM MDT, a severe thunderstorm was located near Veteran, or\n18 miles southwest of Torrington, moving southeast at 20 mph.\n\nHAZARD...Ping pong ball size hail and 60 mph wind gusts.\n\nSOURCE...Public.\n\nIMPACT...People and animals outdoors will be injured. Expect hail\ndamage to roofs, siding, windows, and vehicles. Expect\nwind damage to roofs, siding, and trees.\n\n* Locations impacted include...\nYoder, Veteran, Hawk Springs Reservoir, Hawk Springs State\nRecreation Area, Hawk Springs, and Hawk Springs Campground.",

            "description": "SVRILX\n\nThe National Weather Service in Lincoln has issued a\n\n* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...\nWestern Woodford County in central Illinois...\nNortheastern Tazewell County in central Illinois...\n\n* Until 745 PM CDT.\n\n* At 705 PM CDT, a severe thunderstorm was located near Spring Bay,\nor near Chillicothe, moving southeast at 25 mph.\n\nHAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.\n\nSOURCE...Radar indicated.\n\nIMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected.             "headline": "Special Weather Statement issued June 24 at 7:02PM CDT by NWS Green Bay WI",
            "description": "At 702 PM CDT, Doppler radar was tracking a line of strong\nthunderstorms extending from near Bellevue Town to 5 miles northeast\nof Kaukauna, or extending from near Green Bay to 11 miles east of\nAppleton, moving southeast at 20 mph.\n\nHAZARD...Wind gusts up to 40 mph and penny size hail.\n\nSOURCE...Radar indicated.\n\nIMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around\nunsecured objects. Minor damage to outdoor objects is\npossible.\n\nThe strong thunderstorm will be near...\nBellevue Town, Kaukauna and Little Chute around 705 PM CDT.\nLuxemburg around 720 PM CDT. Brillion around 735 PM CDT. Valders\nand Rawley Point Light around 755 PM CDT.\n\nOther locations impacted by this strong thunderstorm include\nWrightstown, Greenleaf, Lark, Bellevue, Glenmore, Shirley, Uw Green\nBay, New Franken, Bay Settlement and Little Rapids.",
            "instruction": "Monitor the weather situation closely and be alert for threatening\nweather conditions.",
            "response": "Execute",
            "note": null,
            "parameters": {
              "AWIPSidentifier": [
                "SPSGRB"
              ],

            "headline": "Flood Advisory issued June 24 at 7:02PM CDT until June 24 at 10:00PM CDT by NWS Milwaukee/Sullivan WI",
            "description": "* WHAT...Urban and small stream flooding caused by excessive\nrainfall is expected.\n\n* WHERE...Portions of east central, south central, and southeast\nWisconsin, including the following counties, in east central\nWisconsin, Fond du Lac. In south central Wisconsin, Columbia and\nGreen Lake. In southeast Wisconsin, Dodge.\n\n* WHEN...Until 1000 PM CDT.\n\n* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 659 PM CDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to\nthunderstorms. This will cause urban and small stream\nflooding. Between 0.8 and 1.5 inches of rain have fallen in a\nshort period of time and the storms are tracking south-\nsoutheast.\n- Minor street flooding and heavy field flooding was occurring\nin the Waupun area around 6:45 PM.\n- Some locations that will experience flooding include...\nBeaver Dam, Waupun, Mayville, Horicon, Lomira, Randolph,\nTheresa, Oakfield, Cambria, Burnett, Ashford, Byron, Fox\nLake, Alto, Brownsville, Friesland, Kekoskee, Atwater, Oak\nCenter and Astico.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.",

            "description": "SVRMKX\n\nThe National Weather Service in Milwaukee/Sullivan has issued a\n\n* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...\nNortheastern Columbia County in south central Wisconsin...\nNorthwestern Dodge County in southeastern Wisconsin...\n\n* Until 730 PM CDT.\n\n* At 655 PM CDT, a severe thunderstorm was located near Cambria, or\n15 miles east of Portage, moving southeast at 25 mph.\n\nHAZARD...60 mph wind gusts.\n\nSOURCE...Radar indicated.\n\nIMPACT...Expect damage to roofs, siding, and trees.\n\n* Locations impacted include...\nRandolph, Rio, Cambria, Friesland, and Doylestown.",

            "headline": "Special Weather Statement issued June 24 at 5:53PM MDT by NWS North Platte NE",
            "description": "At 553 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm 8\nmiles southwest of Lemoyne, or 13 miles northeast of Big Springs,\nmoving east at 30 mph.\n\nHAZARD...Nickel size hail.\n\nSOURCE...Radar indicated.\n\nIMPACT...Minor hail damage to vegetation is possible.\n\nLocations impacted include...\nOgallala, Lemoyne, Eagle Gulch Campground, and Lake View Campground.\n\nThis includes the following highways...\nHighway 61 between mile markers 89 and 90, and between mile markers\n100 and 102.\nHighway 92 between mile markers 129 and 138.\nInterstate 80 in Nebraska between mile markers 121 and 125.",

            "description": "SMWLOT\n\nThe National Weather Service in Chicago has issued a\n\n* Special Marine Warning for...\n\nNearshore Waters from Wilmette Harbor to Calumet Harbor...\nNearshore Waters from Calumet Harbor to Burns Harbor...\nOpen Waters from Wilmette Harbor to Michigan City out to Mid\nLake...\n\n* Until 845 PM CDT.\n\n* At 638 PM CDT, a severe thunderstorm was located 8 nm west of Ohare\nAirport, or 19 nm west of Wilmette Harbor, moving southeast at 30\nknots.\n\nHAZARD...Wind gusts to 40 knots and large hail.\n\nSOURCE...Radar.\n\nIMPACT...Small craft could be damaged in briefly higher winds and\nsuddenly higher waves.             "instruction": "Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.",

            "headline": "Flash Flood Warning issued June 24 at 5:25PM MDT until June 24 at 8:30PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM",
            "description": "FFWABQ\n\nThe National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a\n\n* Flash Flood Warning for...\nNorth Central Colfax County in northeastern New Mexico...\n\n* Until 830 PM MDT.\n\n* At 525 PM MDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated\nthunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between\n1 and 2 inches of rain have fallen in the past hour. Additional\nrainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible in the warned area.\nFlash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.\n\nHAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.\n\nSOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.\n\nIMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,\nhighways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor\ndrainage and low-lying areas.\n\n* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...\nRaton.\n\nThis includes the following highways...\nHighway 64 between Mile Markers 350 and 351. Interstate 25 between\nMile Markers 450 and 456.",
            "instruction": "Excessive runoff from heavy rainfall will cause flooding of normally\ndry arroyos and streambeds, low water crossings, intersections and\nunderpasses as well as other poor drainage and low lying areas.\n\nTurn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.",

            "headline": "Flood Advisory issued June 24 at 6:23PM CDT until June 24 at 9:30PM CDT by NWS Chicago IL",
            "description": "* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.\n\n* WHERE...A portion of northeast Illinois, including portions of the\nfollowing counties, Cook and Kane.\n\n* WHEN...Until 930 PM CDT.\n\n* IMPACTS...Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.\nRoads and streets may be flooded.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 621 PM CDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to\nthunderstorms with rates of 1 to 2 inches per hour. Up to 1.5\ninches of rain occurred from these storms earlier near\nAlgonquin.\n- Some locations that will experience flooding include...\nChicago, Elgin, Arlington Heights, Schaumburg, Palatine, Des\nPlaines, Mount Prospect, Hoffman Estates, Buffalo Grove,\nBartlett, Streamwood, Hanover Park, Carpentersville,\nWheeling, Elk Grove Village, Algonquin, Huntley, Barrington,\nRolling Meadows and Roselle.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "A Flood Advisory means minor flooding along waterways and other poor\ndrainage areas is imminent or may already be occurring. Persons in\nthe advisory area should use caution and avoid flood waters.",

            "description": "* Affected Area...Fire Weather Zone 424 Southeastern Humboldt\nCounty and northern Lander County, Fire Weather Zone 425 White\nPine and Northeast Nye Counties, Fire Weather Zone 426\nNorthern Nye County-Mojave, Fire Weather Zone 427 Central\nNevada- Toiyabe, Fire Weather Zone 438 W Elko County, N Eureka\nand Lander Counties N of I80, Fire Weather Zone 469 Central\nElko County and Fire Weather Zone 470 Eastern Elko County.\n\n* WIND...Sustained west winds 15 to 25 mph, with gusts 30 to 40\nmph.\n\n* HUMIDITY...Minimum relative humidity values as low as 7\npercent.\n\n* IMPACTS...any fires that develop will likely spread rapidly.\nOutdoor burning is not recommended.",

            "headline": "Flood Advisory issued June 24 at 4:12PM MST until June 24 at 6:15PM MST by NWS Tucson AZ",
            "description": "* WHAT...Urban area and small stream flooding caused by excessive\nrainfall is expected.\n\n* WHERE...Southwestern Cochise County in southeastern Arizona...\n\n* WHEN...Until 615 PM MST.\n\n* IMPACTS...Dangerous flows over low-water crossings. Some low-water\ncrossings may become impassable.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 412 PM MST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to\nthunderstorms. This  will cause urban and small stream flooding.\nBetween 0.5 and 1 inch of rain has fallen.\n- Some locations that will experience flooding include...\nSierra Vista, Hereford, Palominas and Coronado National Memorial.\n- This includes Route 92 between mile markers 333 and 341.\n\nThis includes the following Flash Flood Prone Locations...\nMoson Rd from HWY 90 and Hereford Rd.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nBe aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.",
            "response": "Avoid",

            "headline": "Flood Advisory issued June 24 at 6:09PM CDT until June 24 at 9:15PM CDT by NWS Green Bay WI",
            "description": "Thunderstorms with heavy rain are moving over areas previously\naffected by heavy rain.\n\n* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.\n\n* WHERE...Northwestern Brown County in northeastern Wisconsin...\nNortheastern Outagamie County in northeastern Wisconsin...\nEastern Shawano County in northeastern Wisconsin...\n\n* WHEN...Until 915 PM CDT.\n\n* IMPACTS...Some low-water crossings may become impassable.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 609 PM CDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to\nthunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin\nshortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have\nfallen.\n- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are expected over\nthe area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.\n- Some locations that will experience flooding include...\nGreen Bay, Bellevue Town, Navarino Wildlife Area, Oneida, De\nPere, Howard, Ashwaubenon, Allouez, Hobart, Seymour, Pittsfield,\nNavarino, Nichols, Kunesh, Rose Lawn, Anston, Laney, Hofa Park,\nBriarton and Lambeau Field.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",

            "headline": "Red Flag Warning issued June 24 at 5:07PM MDT until June 24 at 11:00PM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT",
            "description": "* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zone 493 Central Utah Mountains.\n\n* THUNDERSTORMS...Wednesday until 11 PM, Scattered dry\nthunderstorms with numerous outflow wind gusts to around 40 mph\nand isolated widely scattered wind gusts to around 60 mph.\n\n* WINDS...Friday and Saturday, southwest 20 to 30 mph with gusts\n40 to 50 mph with little relief Friday night.\n\n* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Friday and Saturday, as low as 5 percent.\nLittle to no overnight recovery Friday night.\n\n* IMPACTS...Critical fire weather conditions are expected. Any\nnew fire starts or existing fires may spread rapidly.",
            "instruction": "A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions\nare either occurring now...or are imminent. A combination of\nlightning...dry fuel conditions...and gusty microburst winds will\ncreate favorable conditions for new fire starts and extreme fire\nbehavior.\n\nA Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions\nare either occurring now...or are imminent. A combination of\nstrong winds...low relative humidity...and warm temperatures can\ncontribute to extreme fire behavior.",
            "response": "Prepare",

            "description": "* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zone 493 Central Utah Mountains.\n\n* THUNDERSTORMS...Wednesday until 11 PM, Scattered dry\nthunderstorms with numerous outflow wind gusts to around 40 mph\nand isolated widely scattered wind gusts to around 60 mph.\n\n* WINDS...Friday and Saturday, southwest 20 to 30 mph with gusts\n40 to 50 mph with little relief Friday night.\n\n* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Friday and Saturday, as low as 5 percent.\nLittle to no overnight recovery Friday night.\n\n* IMPACTS...Critical fire weather conditions are expected.             "instruction": "A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions\nare either occurring now...or are imminent.             "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Lake Charles LA",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 6:04PM CDT until June 25 at 6:00PM CDT by NWS Lake Charles LA",
            "description": "* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.\n\n* WHERE...A portion of central Louisiana, including the following\nparishes, Avoyelles, Evangeline and St. Landry.\n\n* WHEN...Until 600 PM CDT Thursday.\n\n* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying\nand flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Numerous roads\nremain closed due to flooding. Streams continue to rise due to\nexcess runoff from earlier rainfall. Expect many areas of slow\nmoving or standing water. It will take several hours for all the\nwater from these storms to work through local drainage systems in\nurban areas.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 603 PM CDT, gauge reports indicated runoff and standing\nwater from previous excessive rainfall.\n- Some locations that will experience flooding include...\nMelville, Palmetto, Morrow, Bayou Current, Port Barre,\nLebeau, Big Cane, Goudeau, Dupont and Whiteville.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nKeep children away from storm drains, culverts, creeks and streams.\nWater levels can rise rapidly and sweep children away.\n\nStay away or be swept away. River banks and culverts can become\nunstable and unsafe.",
            "response": "Avoid",
            "note": null,

            "description": "* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.\n\n* WHERE...A portion of southeast Oklahoma, including the following\ncounties, Atoka and Coal.\n\n* WHEN...Until 900 PM CDT.\n\n* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 602 PM CDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to\nthunderstorms.             "headline": "Air Quality Alert issued June 24 at 4:10PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO",
            "description": "The Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment has\nissued the following...\n\nWHAT...Air Quality Health Advisory for Wildfire Smoke.\n\nWHERE...Rio Blanco, Garfield, Eagle, Pitkin, Mesa, Delta,\nGunnison, Montrose, San Miguel, Ouray, Dolores, San Juan,\nMontezuma, La Plata, Hinsdale, Mineral and Saguache Counties.\nLocations include, but are not limited to Meeker, Rangely,\nGlenwood Springs, Eagle, Vail, Aspen, Grand Junction, Delta,\nGunnison, Montrose, Nucla, Telluride, Ouray, Dove Creek,\nSilverton, Cortez, Durango, Hermosa, Honeyville, Rockwood, Lake\nCity, Creede and Saguache.\n\nWHEN...900 AM Wednesday June 24 to 900 AM Thursday June 25\n\nIMPACTS...Smoke from several fires burning in Utah and Nevada is\nbeing transported into Colorado and is expected to impact air\nquality through at least Thursday morning. Smoke levels could\nincrease or decrease rapidly at times during the advisory period\ndue to the very unstable atmospheric conditions.\n\nHEALTH INFORMATION...Public Health Recommendations: If smoke is\nthick or becomes thick in your neighborhood you may want to remain\nindoors. This is especially true for those with heart disease,\nrespiratory illnesses, the very young, and older adults. Consider\nlimiting outdoor activity when moderate to heavy smoke is present.\nConsider relocating temporarily if smoke is present indoors and is\nmaking you ill. If visibility is less than 5 miles in smoke in\nyour neighborhood, smoke has reached levels that are unhealthy.",
            "instruction": null,
            "response": "Monitor",

            "headline": "Air Quality Alert issued June 24 at 4:10PM MDT by NWS Denver CO",
            "description": "The Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment has\nissued the following...\n\nWHAT...Ozone Action Day Alert.\n\nWHERE...Douglas, Jefferson, Denver, western Arapahoe, western\nAdams, Broomfield, Boulder, Larimer, and Weld Counties\n\nWHEN...400 PM Wednesday June 24 to 1200 AM Thursday June 25\n\nIMPACTS...Ozone Action Day Alert is now in effect for the Front\nRange Urban Corridor.  Ozone concentrations in the Unhealthy for\nSensitive Groups category can be expected Wednesday afternoon and\nevening in southern and western parts of the Denver metro area,\nincluding the adjacent foothills. Ozone is expected to be lower\nand within the Good to Moderate range on Thursday due to cooler\ntemperatures and afternoon thunderstorms.  For Colorado air\nquality conditions, forecasts, and advisories, visit:\nhttps://www.colorado.gov/airquality/colorado_summary.aspx   If\npossible, please help us reduce ozone pollution by limiting\ndriving gas and diesel-powered vehicles until midnight, Wednesday\nnight, June 24, 2026. Colorado is also addressing ozone pollution\nthrough state policies. For more information about health impacts\nand how ozone pollution forms in Colorado, visit:\nhttps://cdphe.colorado.gov/ozone- pollution-and-your-health\n\nHEALTH INFORMATION...Increasing likelihood of respiratory symptoms\nand breathing discomfort in active children and adults and people\nwith lung disease, such as asthma. Active children and adults, and\npeople with lung disease, such as asthma, should reduce prolonged\nor heavy outdoor exertion.",

            "event": "Heat Advisory",
            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Seattle WA",
            "headline": "Heat Advisory issued June 24 at 3:02PM PDT until June 24 at 11:00PM PDT by NWS Seattle WA",
            "description": "* WHAT...Warm conditions with high temperatures in the in the 80s\nand lows in the mid 50s to mid 60s. This will pose a moderate risk\nof heat-related illness.\n\n* WHERE...Eastern Kitsap County, City of Seattle, Downtown Everett /\nMarysville Area, Eastside, Foothills and Valleys of Central King\nCounty, Foothills and Valleys of Pierce and Southern King\nCounties, Foothills and Valleys of Snohomish and Northern King\nCounties, Lowlands of Pierce and Southern King Counties, and\nShoreline / Lynnwood / South Everett Area.\n\n* WHEN...Until 11 PM PDT this evening.\n\n* IMPACTS...Heat will significantly increase the risk of\nheat-related illnesses for those who are sensitive to heat,\nespecially those without effective cooling or adequate hydration.",
            "instruction": "Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of\nthe sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors. Young children and\npets should never be left unattended in vehicles under any\ncircumstances.\n\nTake extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When\npossible reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or\nevening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat\nstroke. Wear lightweight and loose fitting clothing when possible.\nTo reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and\nHealth Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in\nshaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat\nshould be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an\nemergency! Call 9 1 1.\n\nFor sheltering information and other human services in your area,\ndial 2 1 1 during business hours or visit wa211.org anytime.",
            "response": "Execute",
            "note": null,
            "parameters": {

                "NPWSEW"
              ],
              "WMOidentifier": [

              ],
              "NWSheadline": [
                "HEAT ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 11 PM PDT THIS EVENING"
              ],

                "EAS",
                "NWEM",
                "CMAS"
              ],

            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Green Bay WI",
            "headline": "Flood Advisory issued June 24 at 5:01PM CDT until June 24 at 8:00PM CDT by NWS Green Bay WI",
            "description": "Slow moving thunderstorms are producing heavy rainfall.\n\n* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.\n\n* WHERE...Southern Oconto County in northeastern Wisconsin...\nEast Central Shawano County in northeastern Wisconsin...\n\n* WHEN...Until 800 PM CDT.\n\n* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 500 PM CDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to\nthunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin\nshortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have\nfallen.\n- Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are expected over the\narea. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.\n- Some locations that will experience flooding include...\nGillett, Bonduel, Underhill, Cecil, Green Valley, Pulcifer,\nAdvance, Zachow, Shawano Lake and Krakow.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.",
            "response": "Avoid",
            "note": null,
            "parameters": {

            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Green Bay WI",
            "headline": "Flood Advisory issued June 24 at 4:50PM CDT until June 24 at 7:45PM CDT by NWS Green Bay WI",
            "description": "Slow moving thunderstorms are producing heavy rain.\n\n* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.\n\n* WHERE...Northern Florence County in northeastern Wisconsin...\nNorthwestern Forest County in northeastern Wisconsin...\n\n* WHEN...Until 745 PM CDT.\n\n* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 450 PM CDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to\nthunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin\nshortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have\nfallen.\n- Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are expected over the\narea. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.\n- Some locations that will experience flooding include...\nFlorence, Tipler, Whisker Lake Wilderness, Commonwealth, Stevens\nLake Campground, Windsor Dam Campground and Luna- White Deer\nCampground.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.",
            "response": "Avoid",
            "note": null,

            "description": "* WHAT...Northwest winds 15 to 25 kt with gusts up to 30 kt and\nseas 7 to 10 feet.\n\n* WHERE...Waters from Cape Mendocino to Pt. Arena CA from 10 to\n60 nm.\n\n* WHEN...Until 3 AM PDT Friday.\n\n* IMPACTS...Conditions will be hazardous to small craft.",

            "event": "Flood Watch",
            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Goodland KS",
            "headline": "Flood Watch issued June 24 at 3:04PM MDT until June 26 at 12:00AM MDT by NWS Goodland KS",
            "description": "Multiple days of heavy rainfall has led to saturated soil across\nmuch of the Tri-State area. Additional rainfall is expected tonight\nthrough Thursday morning and could lead to flash flooding.\n\n* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be\npossible.\n\n* WHERE...Portions of Colorado, including the following areas, Kit\nCarson and Yuma, Kansas, including the following areas, Cheyenne\nKS, Decatur, Gove, Graham, Greeley, Logan, Norton, Rawlins,\nSheridan, Sherman, Thomas, Wallace and Wichita, and southwest\nNebraska, including the following areas, Dundy, Hitchcock and Red\nWillow.\n\n* WHEN...Through Thursday evening.\n\n* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in additional flooding of\nrivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone\nlocations. Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.\nLow-water crossings may be flooded. Extensive street flooding and\nflooding of creeks and rivers are possible. Area creeks and\nstreams are running high and could flood with more heavy rain.",
            "instruction": "You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action\nshould Flash Flood Warnings be issued.",
            "response": "Prepare",
            "note": null,
            "parameters": {
              "AWIPSidentifier": [
                "FFAGLD"
              ],

            "description": "...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in\nKansas...\n\nArkansas River at Arkansas City affecting Cowley County.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Arkansas River at Arkansas City.\n\n* WHEN...Until early tomorrow afternoon.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 11.0 feet, Flooding of agricultural lands can be\nexpected with bank overflows on west side of river. West Chestnut\nAvenue west of the river floods, expect road closure.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 3:00 PM CDT Wednesday the stage was 12.4 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage\njust after midnight tonight and continue falling to 5.2 feet\nearly Monday afternoon.\n- Flood stage is 11.0 feet.",
            "instruction": "Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive\ncars through flooded areas.\n\nDo not drive into flooded areas or go around barricades. Nearly two\nfeet of water will carry most vehicles away.             "senderName": "NWS Phoenix AZ",
            "headline": "Extreme Heat Warning issued June 24 at 1:27PM MST until June 25 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ",
            "description": "* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions. Afternoon temperatures 106 to\n112 degrees. Localized Major Heat Risk.\n\n* WHERE...The lower Colorado River Valley, including the city of\nYuma.\n\n* WHEN...Until 8 PM MST /8 PM PDT/ Thursday.\n\n* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during\nextreme heat events. Overexposure can cause heat cramps and heat\nexhaustion to develop and, without intervention, can lead to heat\nstroke.",
            "instruction": "An Extreme Heat Warning means that a period of very hot temperatures,\neven by local standards, will occur. Actions should be taken to\nlessen the impact of the extreme heat.\n\nTake extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When\npossible, reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or\nevening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat\nstroke. Wear lightweight and loose-fitting clothing when possible and\ndrink plenty of water.\n\nTo reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and\nHealth Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in\nshaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat\nshould be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an\nemergency! Call 9 1 1.\n\nPublic cooling shelters are available in some areas. Consult county\nofficials for more details.",
            "response": "Execute",
            "note": null,

            "senderName": "NWS Tucson AZ",
            "headline": "Extreme Heat Warning issued June 24 at 1:24PM MST until June 25 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Tucson AZ",
            "description": "* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions with afternoon temperatures of\n106 to 109 degrees. Localized Major Heat Risk.\n\n* WHERE...Southeast Pinal County, Tucson Metro Area, Upper Gila River\nValley, and Upper San Pedro River Valley (mainly north of Benson).\n\n* WHEN...Until 8 PM MST Thursday.\n\n* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during\nextreme heat events.",
            "instruction": "To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and\nHealth Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in\nshaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat\nshould be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an\nemergency! Call 9 1 1.\n\nTake extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When\npossible, reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or\nevening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat\nstroke. Wear lightweight and loose fitting clothing when possible and\ndrink plenty of water.",
            "response": "Execute",
            "note": null,

            "headline": "Fire Weather Watch issued June 24 at 1:19PM MST until June 28 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Tucson AZ",
            "description": "The National Weather Service in Tucson has issued a Fire Weather\nWatch for strong and gusty winds, low relative humidity, and high\nto very high fire danger, which is in effect from Saturday\nmorning through Sunday evening.\n\n* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zones 150, 151, 152, 153 and 154.\n\n* TIMING...From 10 AM MST Saturday through 8 PM MST Sunday.\n\n* WINDS...Southwest 15 to 25 mph with gusts up to 35 to 40 mph.\n\n* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...8 to 15 percent.\n\n* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop or are ongoing will have the\npotential to spread rapidly.",
            "instruction": "A Fire Weather Watch means that critical fire weather conditions\nare forecast to occur. Listen for later forecasts and possible\nRed Flag Warnings.\n\nPlease advise the appropriate officials or fire crews in the\nfield of the Fire Weather Watch for portions of Southeast\nArizona.",

            "senderName": "NWS Norman OK",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 3:16PM CDT until June 25 at 7:21PM CDT by NWS Norman OK",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in\nOklahoma...\n\nClear Boggy Creek near Caney affecting Atoka County.\n\n* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and minor flooding is\nforecast.\n\n* WHERE...Clear Boggy Creek near Caney.\n\n* WHEN...Until tomorrow evening.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 29.0 feet, Creek levels rise to three feet higher\nthan flood stage in western Atoka County and the northeastern edge\nof Bryan County. High stages on small feeder streams result in\neven greater depths to mainstem bottomlands near their points of\nentry into Clear Boggy Creek. Croplands... pastures... and some\nsecondary rural roads are flooded.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 2:30 PM CDT Wednesday the stage was 29.3 feet.\n- Bankfull stage is 26.0 feet.\n- Forecast...The Clear Boggy Creek is expected to fall below\nflood stage early tomorrow afternoon and continue falling.\n- Flood stage is 26.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nMotorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive\ncars through flooded areas.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.",
            "response": "Avoid",
            "note": null,

            "senderName": "NWS Fairbanks AK",
            "headline": "Red Flag Warning issued June 24 at 12:15PM AKDT until June 25 at 12:00AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK",
            "description": "The National Weather Service in Fairbanks has issued a Red Flag\nWarning, which is in effect until midnight AKDT tonight.\n\n* AFFECTED AREA...Upper Kobuk Valleys and Lower Koyukuk Valley.\n\n* TIMING...Until midnight AKDT tonight.\n\n* WINDS...Northwest 8 to 15 mph with gusts up to 25 mph.\n\n* HUMIDITY...As low as 20 to 25 percent.\n\n* TEMPERATURES...Highs in the upper 70s to low 80s. Lows in the lower 50s.\n\n* IMPACTS...Critical fire weather conditions are developing\nWednesday due to a combination of hot temperatures, low relative\nhumidity, gusty winds from the west, and dry fuels.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...RH recovery tonight will likely reach above 70\npercent for low lying areas in valleys and along rivers.\nHot and dry conditions continue Thursday with sustained wind\nspeeds likely less than 15 mph.",
            "instruction": "A Red Flag Warning means that conditions are occurring or will\noccur which could lead to the development of large and dangerous\nfires. It is directed toward fire agencies, and through them, to\nthe public.\n\nPlease advise the appropriate officials or fire crews in the\nfield of this Red Flag Warning.",

            "description": "* WHAT...North winds 20 to 30 kt with gusts up to 35 kt and steep\nwind-driven seas of 6 to 10 ft.\n\n* WHERE...All waters south of Cape Blanco.\n\n* WHEN...Until 11 AM PDT Thursday.\n\n* IMPACTS...Gusty winds and/or steep seas could capsize or\ndamage smaller vessels.\n\n* View the hazard area in detail at https://go.usa.gov/x6hks",
            "instruction": "Inexperienced mariners and those operating smaller vessels should\nremain in port and avoid the area of hazardous conditions.",

            "description": "...The National Weather Service in Tulsa OK has issued a Flood\nWarning for the following rivers in Oklahoma...\n\nPolecat Creek near Jenks affecting Tulsa County.\n\nPolecat Creek near Sapulpa affecting Creek County.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Polecat Creek near Sapulpa.\n\n* WHEN...From this evening to tomorrow morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 22.0 feet, minor flooding of pasturelands and oil\nfields occurs.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 12:32 PM CDT Wednesday the stage was 12.0 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage\nthis evening to a crest of 22.5 feet this evening.             "description": "* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions with temperatures up to 110 San\nDiego County Deserts.\n\n* WHERE...San Diego County Deserts.\n\n* WHEN...Until 8 PM PDT Thursday.\n\n* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during\nextreme heat events.",
            "instruction": "Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of\nthe sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.\n\nDo not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles.             "description": "The National Weather Service in Hanford has issued a Fire Weather\nWatch, which is in effect from Friday morning through Saturday\nevening.\n\n* AFFECTED AREA...Fire weather zone Indian Wells Valley.Fire\nweather zone Kern County Desert.Fire weather zone Lake\nIsabella.\n\n* WIND...50 TO 60 PERCENT PROBABILITY OF GUSTS EXCEEDING 55 MPH ON\nFRIDAY IN EASTERN KERN COUNTY. 70 TO 80 PERCENT PROBABILITY OF\nGUSTS EXCEEDING 55 MPH ON SATURDAY IN EASTERN KERN COUNTY. 70 TO\n80 PERCENT PROBABILITY OF GUSTS EXCEEDING 40 MPH AT LAKE\nISABELLA.\n\n* HUMIDITY...EASTERN KERN COUNTY MINIMUM RELATIVE HUMIDITY BETWEEN\n12-20 PERCENT. LAKE ISABELLA MINIMUM RELATIVE HUMIDITY BETWEEN\n25-35 PERCENT.\n\n* THUNDERSTORMS...NO THUNDERSTORM THREAT\n\n\n* IMPACTS...any fires that develop will likely spread rapidly.\nOutdoor burning is not recommended.",
            "instruction": "A Fire Weather Watch means that critical fire weather conditions\nare forecast to occur. Listen for later forecasts and possible\nRed Flag Warnings.",

            "headline": "Flood Watch issued June 24 at 2:17PM CDT until June 26 at 1:00AM CDT by NWS Dodge City KS",
            "description": "The active wet pattern continues across southwest Kansas, with\nanother thunderstorm complex expected late Wednesday night through\nThursday. Topsoils have become saturated, with any additional\nrainfall leading to runoff concerns.\n\n* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be\npossible.\n\n* WHERE...Portions of central, south central, southwest, and west\ncentral Kansas, including the following counties, in central\nKansas, Ellis and Rush. In south central Kansas, Barber, Comanche,\nEdwards, Kiowa, Pawnee, Pratt and Stafford. In southwest Kansas,\nClark, Finney, Ford, Grant, Gray, Hamilton, Haskell, Hodgeman,\nKearny, Meade, Morton, Seward, Stanton and Stevens. In west\ncentral Kansas, Lane, Ness, Scott and Trego.\n\n* WHEN...From 1 AM CDT  /midnight MDT/ Thursday through late\nThursday night.\n\n* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,\ncreeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.\nFlooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Area creeks\nand streams are running high and could flood with more heavy rain.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- Additional rainfall amounts of 1-2 inches are expected to be\ncommon Thursday.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action\nshould Flash Flood Warnings be issued.",
            "response": "Prepare",
            "note": null,

            "headline": "Red Flag Warning issued June 24 at 12:04PM PDT until June 27 at 11:00PM PDT by NWS Reno NV",
            "description": "The National Weather Service in Reno has issued a Red Flag\nWarning for gusty winds and low humidity, which is in effect from\n11 AM Friday to 11 PM PDT Saturday. The Fire Weather Watch has\nbeen upgraded to a Red Flag Warning.\n\n* CHANGES...Fire Weather Watch upgraded to a Red Flag Warning.\n\n* Affected Area...Fire Weather Zone 420 Northern Sierra Front\nincluding Carson City, Douglas, Storey, Southern Washoe,\nWestern Lyon, and Far Southern Lassen Counties.\n\n* Winds...West 20 to 30 mph with gusts up to 45 mph.\n\n* Humidity...Afternoon minimums 12 to 20 percent.\n\n* Duration...2 to 4 hours Friday with 3 to 8 hours Saturday.\nWhile humidity will recover Friday night, winds will stay breezy\non midslopes and ridges.\n\n* Impacts...The combination of gusty winds and low humidity can\ncause fire to rapidly grow in size and intensity before first\nresponders can contain them, especially from any recent\nlightning holdovers.",
            "instruction": "Avoid outdoor activities that can cause a spark near dry\nvegetation, such as yard work, target shooting, or campfires.\nFollow local fire restrictions. Check weather.gov/reno for\nupdates and livingwithfire.info for preparedness tips.",

            "headline": "Flood Watch issued June 24 at 2:02PM CDT until June 26 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Wichita KS",
            "description": "* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be\npossible.\n\n* WHERE...Portions of central, east central, south central, and\nsoutheast Kansas, including the following counties, in central\nKansas, Barton, Ellsworth, Lincoln, Marion, McPherson, Rice,\nRussell and Saline. In east central Kansas, Chase. In south\ncentral Kansas, Butler, Cowley, Harper, Harvey, Kingman, Reno,\nSedgwick and Sumner. In southeast Kansas, Allen, Chautauqua, Elk,\nGreenwood, Labette, Montgomery, Neosho, Wilson and Woodson.\n\n* WHEN...From 1 AM CDT Thursday through Friday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,\ncreeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.\nCreeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur\nin poor drainage and urban areas.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- Several rounds of thunderstorms producing heavy rainfall are\nexpected from late tonight through early Friday morning.\nWhile not everyone will see flooding from rainfall, it\nappears likely that several locations will receive enough\nrainfall to cause flooding concerns.",
            "instruction": "Do not drive into flooded areas or go around barricades. Nearly two\nfeet of water will carry most vehicles away. Turn around, don't\ndrown.\n\nBe aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.",

            "headline": "Fire Weather Watch issued June 24 at 1:01PM MDT until June 28 at 12:00AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO",
            "description": "The National Weather Service in Grand Junction has issued a Red\nFlag Warning for gusty winds, low relative humidity and dry\nfuels, which is in effect from noon to 9 PM MDT Friday. A Fire\nWeather Watch has also been issued. This Fire Weather Watch for\ngusty winds, low relative humidity and dry fuels is in effect\nfrom Saturday morning through Saturday evening. The Fire Weather\nWatch is no longer in effect.\n\n* AFFECTED AREA...In Colorado, Fire Weather Zone 200 Little\nSnake Forecast Area, Fire Weather Zone 202 White River\nForecast Area, Fire Weather Zone 207 Southwest Colorado Lower\nForecast Area and Fire Weather Zone 290 Paradox Valley\nForecast Area.\n\n* TIMING...For the Red Flag Warning, from noon to 9 PM MDT\nFriday. For the Fire Weather Watch, from Saturday morning\nthrough Saturday evening.\n\n* WINDS...Southwest 25 to 35 mph with gusts up to 55 mph.\n\n* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...9 to 14 percent.\n\n* IMPACTS...Elevated fire danger is expected. Fires will catch\nand spread rapidly and erratically.",
            "instruction": "A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions\nare either occurring now, or will shortly.             "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 1:54PM CDT until June 26 at 3:00AM CDT by NWS Wichita KS",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Kansas...\n\nCow Creek near Hutchinson affecting Reno and Rice Counties.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Cow Creek near Hutchinson.\n\n* WHEN...Until early Friday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 10.0 feet, The low water crossing on Wilson Rd\nbetween 69th Ave to 82nd Ave floods. Expect water depth near 4\ninches to a width of 5 feet.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 1:15 PM CDT Wednesday the stage was 9.6 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 9.9\nfeet just after midnight tonight. It will then fall below\nflood stage tomorrow afternoon.\n- Flood stage is 9.5 feet.",
            "instruction": "Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive\ncars through flooded areas.\n\nDo not drive into flooded areas or go around barricades. Nearly two\nfeet of water will carry most vehicles away.             "senderName": "NWS Cheyenne WY",
            "headline": "Flash Flood Watch issued June 24 at 12:53PM MDT until June 26 at 12:00AM MDT by NWS Cheyenne WY",
            "description": "* WHAT...Flash flooding and debris flows caused by excessive\nrainfall are possible over the South Fork Burn Scar Area.\n\n* WHERE...The South Fork Burn Scar Area in the northern Nebraska\npanhandle and downstream areas along Soldier Creek and the White\nRiver, including Fort Robinson and Crawford.\n\n* WHEN...Through Thursday evening.\n\n* IMPACTS...Localized thunderstorm heavy rainfall over the South\nFork Burn Scar Area is possible. Multiple rounds of thunderstorms\nare expected in the area through Thursday evening. Residents near\nthe South Fork Burn Scar Area should prepare for potential\nflooding impacts. Be sure to stay up to date with information from\nlocal authorities. Heavy rainfall could trigger flash flooding of\nlow-lying areas, urbanized street flooding, and debris flows in\nand near recent wildfire burn scars.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- National Weather Service Meteorologists are forecasting\nlocally heavy rainfall over the burn scar, which may lead to\nflash flooding and debris flows.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action\nshould Flash Flood Warnings be issued.",
            "response": "Monitor",
            "note": null,

            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Goodland KS",
            "headline": "Flood Advisory issued June 24 at 1:50PM CDT until June 28 at 11:01PM CDT by NWS Goodland KS",
            "description": "...The National Weather Service in Goodland has issued a Flood\nAdvisory for the following rivers in Kansas...\n\nSappa Creek At Oberlin 1sw affecting Decatur County.\n\n.Rainfall over the past several days has lead to river rises. Sappa\nCreek at Oberlin did fall below flood stage this morning, but may\nreturn to flooding with additional rainfall tonight. Please report\nany  river flooding to the National Weather Service.\n\nFor the Sappa Creek...including Norcatur 15ne, Oberlin 1sw...\nelevated river levels are forecast.\n\n* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.\n\n* WHERE...Sappa Creek at Oberlin 1sw.\n\n* WHEN...From Thursday afternoon to late Sunday evening.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 11.0 feet, Water spreads over agricultural fields and\nlow lying areas with actual water depth in creek at about 6 feet.\nAt 15.0 feet, Moderate flooding will occur in nearby agricultural\nfields and low lying areas.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:00 AM CDT Wednesday the stage was 10.0 feet.\n- Bankfull stage is 11.0 feet.\n- Forecast...The river may rise above flood stage tomorrow\nafternoon to a crest of 15.4 feet early Friday afternoon. It\nwill then fall below flood stage late Saturday evening.\n- Action stage is 9.0 feet.\n- Flood stage is 11.0 feet.",
            "instruction": "If you are in the advisory area, remain alert to possible flooding\nor the possibility of the advisory being upgraded to a warning.\n\nStay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,\ntelevision, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.\n\nThe next statement will be issued beforeThursday afternoon at 100 PM\nCDT.",
            "response": "Avoid",
            "note": null,

            "senderName": "NWS Spokane WA",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 11:31AM PDT until June 27 at 11:19PM PDT by NWS Spokane WA",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in\nWashington...\n\nStehekin River at Stehekin affecting Chelan County.\n\nFor the Stehekin River...including Stehekin...Minor flooding is\nforecast.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Stehekin River at Stehekin.\n\n* WHEN...Until late Saturday evening.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 20.5 feet, Water inundates some properties and\novertops the temporary corduroy bridge. Company Creek Road\ninundated at northern end. Battalion Creek culverts are beginning\nto be overtopped. Water begins damaging Wood Road.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 10:30 AM PDT Wednesday the stage was 20.7 feet.\n- Bankfull stage is 19.5 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours\nending at 10:30 AM PDT Wednesday was 20.8 feet.\n- Forecast...The river will fluctuate between 20.6 and 20.9\nfeet through Thursday. It will fall begin falling, and\ndropping flood stage this weekend.\n- Flood stage is 20.5 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive\ncars through flooded areas.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.\n\nThe next statement will be issued Thursday afternoon at 1215 PM PDT.",
            "response": "Avoid",
            "note": null,

            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Pocatello ID",
            "headline": "Red Flag Warning issued June 24 at 12:17PM MDT until June 26 at 12:00AM MDT by NWS Pocatello ID",
            "description": "...RED FLAG WARNING IN EFFECT FROM 9 AM THURSDAY TO MIDNIGHT MDT\nTHURSDAY NIGHT FOR SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS FOR FIRE WEATHER ZONE\n413...\n\nThe National Weather Service in Pocatello has issued a Red Flag\nWarning for scattered thunderstorms, which is in effect from 9 AM\nThursday to midnight MDT Thursday night.\n\n* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zone 413 Caribou Range/Caribou NF.\n\n* IMPACTS...Critical fire weather conditions are expected.\nLightning may generate new fire starts. Any new fire starts or\nexisting fires may spread rapidly\n\n* THUNDERSTORMS...25 to 35 percent coverage.\n\n* OUTFLOW WINDS...35 to 55 mph.",
            "instruction": "A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions\nare either occurring now, or will shortly based on these criteria\nfor Southeastern Idaho:\n\n- Relative humidity at or below 15 percent and wind gusts of at\nleast 25 mph in the mountains, or 30 mph in the Snake Plain.\n\n- Thunderstorm coverage of 25 percent, without specific rainfall\ncriteria.\n\n- Other high impact events deemed critical by the National\nWeather Service and area fire management agencies.",
            "response": "Prepare",
            "note": null,
            "parameters": {
