            "event": "Flood Watch",
            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Tulsa OK",
            "headline": "Flood Watch issued June 24 at 1:16PM CDT until June 26 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Tulsa OK",
            "description": "* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be\npossible.\n\n* WHERE...Portions of east central, northeast, and southeast\nOklahoma, including the following counties, in east central\nOklahoma, Central and Southern Sequoyah, Cherokee, Muskogee,\nNorthern Sequoyah and Okfuskee. In northeast Oklahoma, Adair,\nCraig, Creek, Delaware, Mayes, Northeast Osage, Nowata, Okmulgee,\nOttawa, Pawnee, Rogers, Southeast Osage, Tulsa, Wagoner,\nWashington OK and Western Osage. In southeast Oklahoma, Central Le\nFlore, Haskell, Latimer, McIntosh, Northern Le Flore, Pittsburg\nand Southern Le Flore.\n\n* WHEN...Through Friday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,\ncreeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- Scattered showers and storms will remain possible through the\nafternoon and evening Wednesday. Given saturated ground and\nhigh runoff, will maintain a watch through the afternoon and\nevening across northeast Oklahoma. More widespread\nthunderstorm development is likely late Wednesday night\nthrough the day Thursday. Heavy rainfall rates of one to two\ninches per hour are likely, leading to more flooding\npotential.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood\nWarnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared\nto take action should flooding develop.",
            "response": "Prepare",
            "note": null,
            "parameters": {
              "AWIPSidentifier": [

              ],

            "event": "Heat Advisory",
            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA",
            "headline": "Heat Advisory issued June 24 at 11:04AM PDT until June 24 at 9:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA",
            "description": "* WHAT...Unseasonably hot conditions with temperatures in the mid to\nupper 80s possible in Downtown Los Angeles and upper 70s in\nInglewood area.\n\n* WHERE...Los Angeles County Inland Coast including Downtown Los\nAngeles.\n\n* WHEN...Until 9 PM PDT this evening.\n\n* IMPACTS...There is a high risk for heat illness for sensitive\npopulations including the very young, the very old, those without\nair conditioning, and those active outdoors.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Higher humidity will have the potential to\nadd to the heat discomfort.",
            "instruction": "Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of\nthe sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.\n\nTake extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose\nfitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning\nor evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and\nheat stroke.",
            "response": "Execute",
            "note": null,
            "parameters": {
              "AWIPSidentifier": [

              ],
              "WMOidentifier": [

            "senderName": "NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA",
            "headline": "Heat Advisory issued June 24 at 11:04AM PDT until June 25 at 9:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA",
            "description": "* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions with temperatures in the low to\nmid 90s. Locally in the upper 90s.\n\n* WHERE...Eastern San Fernando Valley, Eastern San Gabriel\nMountains, Los Angeles County San Gabriel Valley, Santa Clarita\nValley, Western San Fernando Valley, and Western San Gabriel\nMountains and Highway 14 Corridor.\n\n* WHEN...Until 9 PM PDT Thursday.\n\n* IMPACTS...There is a high risk for heat illness for sensitive\npopulations including the very young, the very old, those without\nair conditioning, and those active outdoors.",
            "instruction": "Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of\nthe sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.\n\nTake extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose\nfitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning\nor evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and\nheat stroke.",
            "response": "Execute",
            "note": null,

            "headline": "Red Flag Warning issued June 24 at 11:00AM PDT until June 25 at 9:00PM PDT by NWS Spokane WA",
            "description": "...WARM, WINDY AND DRY THURSDAY...\n\nThe National Weather Service in Spokane has issued a Red Flag\nWarning for wind and low relative humidity, which is in effect\nfrom noon to 9 PM PDT Thursday. The Fire Weather Watch is no\nlonger in effect.\n\n* Affected Area: Colville Reservation (Zone 702), Okanogan\nValley (Zone 703), Foothills of Central Washington Cascades\n(Zone 705), Waterville Plateau (Zone 706), Western Columbia\nBasin (Zone 707), Eastern Columbia Basin  -Palouse  -Spokane\nArea (Zone 708) and Lower Palouse  -Snake River (Zone 709).\n\n* Winds: Southwest 10 to 20 mph with gusts up to 30 mph.\n\n* Relative Humidities: 12 to 20 percent.\n\n* Impacts: Rapid fire spread is likely with any new or ongoing\nfires.",
            "instruction": "A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions\nare either occurring now....or will shortly. A combination of\nstrong winds...low relative humidity...and warm temperatures can\ncontribute to extreme fire behavior.",

            "description": "...Breezy winds and low relative humidity expected Thursday...\n\n.The combination of breezy winds and low relative humidity is\nexpected to generate weather conditions conducive to rapid fire\nspread for new and existing fires in the lower Columbia Basin,\nYakima and Kittitas valleys, and the Warm Springs Reservation.\n\nThe National Weather Service in Pendleton has issued a Red Flag\nWarning for wind and low relative humidity, which is in effect\nfrom noon to 9 PM PDT Thursday.             "instruction": "A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions\nare either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of\nstrong winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can\ncontribute to extreme fire behavior.",

            "headline": "Flood Watch issued June 24 at 12:46PM CDT until June 25 at 1:00PM CDT by NWS Little Rock AR",
            "description": "* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.\n\n* WHERE...Portions of central, southwest, and western Arkansas,\nincluding the following areas, in central Arkansas, Garland. In\nsouthwest Arkansas, Clark, Hot Spring and Pike. In western\nArkansas, Central and Eastern Montgomery County, Central and\nSouthern Scott County, Northern Montgomery County Higher\nElevations, Northern Polk County Higher Elevations, Northern Scott\nCounty, Polk County Lower Elevations, Southeast Polk County Higher\nElevations and Southwest Montgomery County Higher Elevations.\n\n* WHEN...Through Thursday afternoon.\n\n* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,\ncreeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- Forecast rainfall amounts of two to four inches will be\npossible over portions of western to southwest Arkansas and\nmuch of the Ouachita Mountains. Local high-end rainfall\namounts greater than four inches will be possible as well. In\naddition to forecast rainfall, much of the area received one\nto two inches of rainfall Wednesday afternoon, resulting in\nprimed soils for runoff and flash flooding.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action\nshould Flash Flood Warnings be issued.",

            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 12:37PM CDT until June 25 at 4:00PM CDT by NWS Lake Charles LA",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...\nLouisiana...\n\nPine Island Bayou Near Sour Lake\n\nCalcasieu River Near Glenmora\n\nCalcasieu River near White Oak Park\n\n...The Flood Warning is cancelled for the following rivers in\nLouisiana...\n\nCalcasieu River Near Oberlin\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Pine Island Bayou near Sour Lake.\n\n* WHEN...Until tomorrow afternoon.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 25.0 feet, Water inundates roads in lowland areas\nnear the river. Low spots on Old Sour Lake Road are under water.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 11:45 AM CDT Wednesday the stage was 25.3 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours\nending at 11:45 AM CDT Wednesday was 25.6 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 25.4\nfeet this afternoon. It will then fall below flood stage late\ntonight.\n- Flood stage is 25.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",

            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 12:37PM CDT by NWS Lake Charles LA",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...\nLouisiana...\n\nPine Island Bayou Near Sour Lake\n\nCalcasieu River Near Glenmora\n\nCalcasieu River near White Oak Park\n\n...The Flood Warning is cancelled for the following rivers in\nLouisiana...\n\nCalcasieu River Near Oberlin\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Calcasieu River near White Oak Park.\n\n* WHEN...Until further notice.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Goos Ferry Road becomes impassable.\nCalcasieu River from the Saltwater Barrier to the parish line may\nbe closed to recreational boat traffic.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 11:35 AM CDT Wednesday the stage was 3.7 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours\nending at 11:35 AM CDT Wednesday was 4.1 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to fall to 2.3 feet Monday\nmorning.\n- Flood stage is 2.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",

            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 12:37PM CDT by NWS Lake Charles LA",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...\nLouisiana...\n\nPine Island Bayou Near Sour Lake\n\nCalcasieu River Near Glenmora\n\nCalcasieu River near White Oak Park\n\n...The Flood Warning is cancelled for the following rivers in\nLouisiana...\n\nCalcasieu River Near Oberlin\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Calcasieu River near Glenmora.\n\n* WHEN...Until further notice.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 14.0 feet, Some roads upstream from Glenmora,\nincluding Strothers Crossing Road near the community of Calcasieu\nand Price Crossing Road near Hineston have two to three feet of\nwater over the road and are subject to being closed. Flooding of\nforested areas near the river will also occur.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 11:45 AM CDT Wednesday the stage was 13.6 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours\nending at 11:45 AM CDT Wednesday was 13.8 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 13.6\nfeet this afternoon.\n- Flood stage is 12.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",

            "event": "Flood Warning",
            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Little Rock AR",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 12:35PM CDT until June 29 at 1:00PM CDT by NWS Little Rock AR",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nArkansas...\n\nCache River Near Patterson affecting Jackson and Woodruff\nCounties.\n\nFor the Cache River...including Patterson...Minor flooding is\nforecast.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Cache River near Patterson.\n\n* WHEN...Until early Monday afternoon.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 9.0 feet, Low swampy timberland along the river\nbegins to flood. Flood gates should be closed and equipment moved\nout of the low grounds along the river and tributaries.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 12:15 PM CDT Wednesday the stage was 9.3 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 9.4\nfeet Wednesday afternoon. It will then fall below flood stage\nSunday morning.\n- Flood stage is 9.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive\ncars through flooded areas.\n\nRiver forecasts are based on current conditions and rainfall\nforecasted to occur over the next 24 hours. During periods of\nflooding...Evening forecasts are reissued with updated rainfall\nforecasts.\n\nObserved and forecasted stage data plots are available on our\nAdvanced Hydrologic Prediction Service web page at...\nwww.weather.gov/lzk\n\nUnder the Current Conditions section...Select River and Lakes AHPS.\n\nThe next statement will be issued Thursday afternoon at 1245 PM CDT.",
            "response": "Avoid",
            "note": null,
            "parameters": {

            "senderName": "NWS Lincoln IL",
            "headline": "Flood Watch issued June 24 at 11:58AM CDT until June 27 at 1:00PM CDT by NWS Lincoln IL",
            "description": "Wet antecedent conditions from recent active weather means that it\nwill not take much additional rainfall for flooding to occur,\nespecially in low lying areas.  Current forecast guidance exhibits a\nhigh (greater than 70%) probability of exceeding 2 inches of\nrainfall within the watch area.\n\n* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.\n\n* WHERE...Portions of central, east central, and southeast Illinois,\nincluding the following counties, in central Illinois, Christian\nand Shelby. In east central Illinois, Clark, Coles, Cumberland and\nMoultrie. In southeast Illinois, Clay, Crawford, Effingham,\nJasper, Lawrence and Richland.\n\n* WHEN...From Thursday afternoon through Saturday afternoon.\n\n* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,\ncreeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood\nWarnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared\nto take action should flooding develop.",
            "response": "Prepare",
            "note": null,

            "headline": "Flood Watch issued June 24 at 11:53AM CDT until June 26 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Topeka KS",
            "description": "* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.\n\n* WHERE...Portions of central, east central, north central, and\nnortheast Kansas, including the following counties, in central\nKansas, Dickinson. In east central Kansas, Anderson, Coffey,\nDouglas, Franklin, Geary, Lyon, Morris, Osage, Shawnee and\nWabaunsee. In north central Kansas, Ottawa. In northeast Kansas,\nJefferson.\n\n* WHEN...From Thursday afternoon through Friday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,\ncreeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- Forecast rainfall amounts of one to three inches Thursday and\nThursday night could lead to scattered flooding, mainly of\narea creeks, streams and rivers.",
            "instruction": "You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood\nWarnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared\nto take action should flooding develop.",

            "description": "* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.\n\n* WHERE...Portions of Illinois, including the following areas, Bond\nIL, Calhoun IL, Clinton IL, Fayette IL, Greene IL, Jersey IL,\nMacoupin IL, Madison IL, Marion IL, Monroe IL, Montgomery IL, Saint\nClair IL and Washington IL and Missouri, including the following\nareas, Boone MO, Callaway MO, Cole MO, Crawford MO, Franklin MO,\nGasconade MO, Jefferson MO, Lincoln MO, Moniteau MO, Montgomery MO,\nOsage MO, Saint Charles MO, Saint Louis City MO, Saint Louis MO,\nWarren MO and Washington MO.\n\n* WHEN...From Thursday afternoon through Friday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,\ncreeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- Multiple waves of thunderstorms capable of heavy rainfall.\n- Some locations that may experience flooding include...\nSt. Louis, Columbia, O'Fallon, St. Charles, St. Peters,\nFlorissant, Chesterfield, Belleville, Jefferson City, Wildwood,\nUniversity City, Ballwin, Granite City, Wentzville, Alton,\nKirkwood, Maryland Heights, East St. Louis and Hazelwood.",
            "instruction": "You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action\nshould Flash Flood Warnings be issued.",
            "response": "Prepare",
            "note": null,

            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Shreveport LA",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 11:43AM CDT until June 27 at 9:00AM CDT by NWS Shreveport LA",
            "description": "...Forecast flooding changed from Minor to Moderate severity and\nincreased in duration for the following rivers in Louisiana...\n\nBayou D'arbonne At Lake Claiborne affecting Claiborne Parish.\n\nFor the Bayou D'arbonne...including Lake Claiborne...Moderate\nflooding is forecast.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is\nforecast.\n\n* WHERE...Bayou D'arbonne at Lake Claiborne.\n\n* WHEN...From this morning to Saturday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 187.5 feet, Expect flooding of some camps. Also boats\nshould be moved from boathouses to avoid boat damage due to rising\nwater. Some secondary roadways will also be flooded and travel\naround the lake will be difficult.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 11:00 AM CDT Wednesday the stage was 188.1 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 189.0 feet\ntomorrow morning. It will then fall below flood stage Friday\nafternoon.\n- Flood stage is 188.0 feet.\n- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 189.1\nfeet on 04/14/2019.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Do not drive cars through flooded areas. Caution is urged when\nwalking near riverbanks. Turn around, don't drown when encountering\nflooded roads. Most flood deaths occur in vehicles.\n\nFor more hydrologic information, copy and paste the following website\naddress into your favorite web browser URL bar:\nhttps://water.noaa.gov/wfo/SHV\n\nThe next statement will be issued Thursday morning at 1145 AM CDT.",
            "response": "Avoid",

            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Shreveport LA",
            "headline": "Flood Watch issued June 24 at 11:19AM CDT until June 25 at 1:00PM CDT by NWS Shreveport LA",
            "description": "* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be\npossible.\n\n* WHERE...Portions of Arkansas, including the following counties,\nColumbia, Hempstead, Howard, Lafayette, Little River, Miller,\nNevada, Sevier and Union, Louisiana, including the following\nparishes, Bienville, Bossier, Caddo, Caldwell, Claiborne, De Soto,\nJackson, Lincoln, Ouachita, Red River, Union, Webster and Winn,\nsoutheast Oklahoma, including the following county, McCurtain, and\nnortheast Texas, including the following counties, Bowie, Camp,\nCass, Franklin, Harrison, Marion, Morris, Red River and Titus.\n\n* WHEN...Through Thursday afternoon.\n\n* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,\ncreeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.\nFlooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- Additional showers and thunderstorms are expected to redevelop\nthis morning through at least early Thursday over portions of\nNortheast Texas, Southeast Oklahoma, Southwest Arkansas, and\nNorth Louisiana, over already saturated soils from heavy rainfall\nthat has fallen over the last several days. These showers and\nthunderstorms will continue the threat for heavy rainfall and\nflash flooding. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches,\nwith isolated higher amounts, are possible across much of the\nWatch area.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood\nWarnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared\nto take action should flooding develop.",
            "response": "Prepare",
            "note": null,

            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 10:39AM CDT until June 25 at 4:36PM CDT by NWS Jackson MS",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nMississippi...\n\nPearl River At Jackson affecting Rankin and Hinds Counties.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Pearl River at Jackson.\n\n* WHEN...Until tomorrow afternoon.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 29.0 feet, Farmland in southern Rankin County begins\nto flood and water begins to affect home access near the river in\nthe Byram area.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 9:30 AM CDT Wednesday the stage was 29.1 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to continue a slow fall.\n- Flood stage is 28.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive\ncars through flooded areas.\n\nTurn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads.             "senderName": "NWS New Orleans LA",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 10:29AM CDT until July 3 at 5:48PM CDT by NWS New Orleans LA",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in\nLouisiana...Mississippi...\n\nPearl River Near Bogalusa affecting Pearl River County and\nWashington Parish.\n\nPearl River Near Pearl River affecting St. Tammany Parish, Hancock\nand Pearl River Counties.\n\nFor the Lower Pearl River...including Bogalusa, Pearl River...Minor\nflooding is forecast.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Pearl River near Bogalusa.\n\n* WHEN...Until Friday, July 03.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 20.0 feet, Woodlands and crop acreage along the river\nwill be flooded. The Bogue Chitto Wildlife Management area will be\ninundated with water in recreational camps and over access roads.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 10:15 AM CDT Wednesday the stage was 19.2 feet.\n- Bankfull stage is 15.0 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending\nat 10:15 AM CDT Wednesday was 19.2 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 20.0 feet\nearly Sunday afternoon then begin falling.\n- Flood stage is 18.0 feet.\n- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 20.0\nfeet on 02/14/2021.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nMotorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars\nthrough flooded areas.\n\nPlease report observed flooding to local emergency services or law\nenforcement and request they pass this information to the National\nWeather Service when you can do so safely.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov/lix.  Click on\nthe Rivers and Lakes menu for forecasts and observations.\n\nThe next statement will be issued when updates are needed.",

            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS New Orleans LA",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 10:29AM CDT until July 3 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS New Orleans LA",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in\nLouisiana...Mississippi...\n\nPearl River Near Bogalusa affecting Pearl River County and\nWashington Parish.\n\nPearl River Near Pearl River affecting St. Tammany Parish, Hancock\nand Pearl River Counties.\n\nFor the Lower Pearl River...including Bogalusa, Pearl River...Minor\nflooding is forecast.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Pearl River near Pearl River.\n\n* WHEN...Until Friday, July 03.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 15.5 feet, Secondary roads to the river and throughout\nHoney Island Swamp are inundated. Property in the vicinity of the\ngage is flooded threatening about 20 homes along the left bank. The\nBogue Chitto National Wildlife Refuge will be closed to hunting at\nthe 15.5 foot stage.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 10:00 AM CDT Wednesday the stage was 15.3 feet.\n- Bankfull stage is 12.0 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending\nat 10:00 AM CDT Wednesday was 15.4 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 15.3 feet\nthis afternoon then begin falling.\n- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.\n- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 15.3\nfeet on 02/10/1956.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nMotorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars\nthrough flooded areas.\n\nPlease report observed flooding to local emergency services or law\nenforcement and request they pass this information to the National\nWeather Service when you can do so safely.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov/lix.  Click on\nthe Rivers and Lakes menu for forecasts and observations.\n\nThe next statement will be issued when updates are needed.",

            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 10:16AM CDT until June 27 at 11:00PM CDT by NWS Paducah KY",
            "description": "...The National Weather Service in Paducah KY has issued a Flood\nWarning for the following rivers in Indiana...Illinois...\n\nWabash River at New Harmony.\n\n.Recent heavy rainfall is continuing to cause rises on the Wabash\nRiver.  At New Harmony, the river will climb above flood stage this\nevening, cresting around a half foot above flood stage Friday.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Wabash River at New Harmony.\n\n* WHEN...From this evening to late Saturday evening.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 9:30 AM CDT Wednesday the stage was 14.6 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage\nlate this evening to a crest of 15.5 feet early Friday\nmorning. It will then fall below flood stage Saturday\nafternoon.\n- Flood stage is 15.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.",

            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 10:12AM CDT until June 25 at 1:00AM CDT by NWS Mobile AL",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following river in Florida...\n\nShoal River Near Crestview affecting Okaloosa County.\n\nFor the Shoal River...including Crestview...Minor flooding is\nforecast.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov/mob.             "senderName": "NWS Pueblo CO",
            "headline": "Air Quality Alert issued June 24 at 9:10AM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO",
            "description": "The Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment has\nissued the following...\n\nWHAT...Air Quality Health Advisory for Wildfire Smoke.\n\nWHERE...Rio Blanco, Garfield, Eagle, Pitkin, Mesa, Delta,\nGunnison, Montrose, San Miguel, Ouray, Dolores, San Juan,\nMontezuma, La Plata, Hinsdale, Mineral and Saguache Counties.\nLocations include, but are not limited to Meeker, Rangely,\nGlenwood Springs, Eagle, Vail, Aspen, Grand Junction, Delta,\nGunnison, Montrose, Nucla, Telluride, Ouray, Dove Creek,\nSilverton, Cortez, Durango, Hermosa, Honeyville, Rockwood, Lake\nCity, Creede and Saguache.\n\nWHEN...900 AM Wednesday June 24 to 900 AM Thursday June 25\n\nIMPACTS...Smoke from several fires burning in Utah and Nevada is\nbeing transported into Colorado and is expected to impact air\nquality through at least Thursday morning. Smoke levels could\nincrease or decrease rapidly at times during the advisory period\ndue to the very unstable atmospheric conditions.\n\nHEALTH INFORMATION...Public Health Recommendations: If smoke is\nthick or becomes thick in your neighborhood you may want to remain\nindoors. This is especially true for those with heart disease,\nrespiratory illnesses, the very young, and older adults. Consider\nlimiting outdoor activity when moderate to heavy smoke is present.\nConsider relocating temporarily if smoke is present indoors and is\nmaking you ill. If visibility is less than 5 miles in smoke in\nyour neighborhood, smoke has reached levels that are unhealthy.",
            "instruction": null,
            "response": "Monitor",
            "note": "Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.",

            "event": "Flood Warning",
            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Indianapolis IN",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 11:08AM EDT until June 27 at 2:00PM EDT by NWS Indianapolis IN",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Indiana...\nIllinois...\n\nWhite River at Hazleton.\n\nWhite River at Petersburg.\n\nWabash River at Riverton.\n\nWabash River at Hutsonville Legacy Power Plant Site.\n\n...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in\nIllinois...Indiana...\n\nWabash River at Mount Carmel.\n\nWabash River at Vincennes.\n\n.Minor flooding continues on the White River from Petersburg\ndown to the Wabash...and on the Wabash River from the Hutsonville\narea down to Mount Carmel. The crest on the White was near Hazleton\nwhile the crest on the Wabash was near Vincennes late Wednesday\nmorning.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Wabash River at Mount Carmel.\n\n* WHEN...Until early Saturday afternoon.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 20.0 feet, River is bankfull in all locations.  All\noil field production ceases with the exception of pumping units on\nsubstructures.  Access to these are by boat only.  Agricultural\nlosses increase dramatically.  Farmers move livestock to higher\nground.  City of Mount Carmel leaves flood gates B and C in year\nround.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 9:45 AM EDT Wednesday /8:45 AM CDT Wednesday/ the stage\nwas 19.5 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours\nending at 9:45 AM EDT Wednesday /8:45 AM CDT Wednesday/ was\n19.5 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 20.1\nfeet tomorrow morning. It will then fall below flood stage\nearly Saturday morning.\n- Flood stage is 19.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov/ind.\n\nThe next statement should be issued this evening by around 1100 PM\nEDT /1000 PM CDT/.",
            "response": "Avoid",
            "note": null,
            "parameters": {
              "AWIPSidentifier": [
                "FLSIND"
              ],
              "WMOidentifier": [
                "WGUS83 KIND 241508"
              ],
              "NWSheadline": [
                "FLOOD WARNING NOW IN EFFECT UNTIL EARLY SATURDAY AFTERNOON"

            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Indianapolis IN",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 11:08AM EDT until June 26 at 1:08AM EDT by NWS Indianapolis IN",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Indiana...\nIllinois...\n\nWhite River at Hazleton.\n\nWhite River at Petersburg.\n\nWabash River at Riverton.\n\nWabash River at Hutsonville Legacy Power Plant Site.\n\n...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in\nIllinois...Indiana...\n\nWabash River at Mount Carmel.\n\nWabash River at Vincennes.\n\n.Minor flooding continues on the White River from Petersburg\ndown to the Wabash...and on the Wabash River from the Hutsonville\narea down to Mount Carmel. The crest on the White was near Hazleton\nwhile the crest on the Wabash was near Vincennes late Wednesday\nmorning.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Wabash River at Riverton.\n\n* WHEN...Until early Friday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 18.0 feet, Extensive lowland flooding is in\nprogress.  High water surrounds many river cabins.  Access to most\nriver cabins is by boat only.  Levees begin to protect farmland.\nExtensive flooding of Leaverton Park occurs in Palestine, Illinois.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 10:00 AM EDT Wednesday /9:00 AM CDT Wednesday/ the stage\nwas 17.7 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours\nending at 10:00 AM EDT Wednesday /9:00 AM CDT Wednesday/ was\n18.4 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage\nearly tomorrow afternoon and continue falling and remain\nbelow flood stage.\n- Flood stage is 15.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov/ind.\n\nThe next statement should be issued this evening by around 1100 PM\nEDT /1000 PM CDT/.",

            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov/ind.\n\nThe next statement should be issued this evening by around 1100 PM\nEDT /1000 PM CDT/.",

            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Indianapolis IN",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 11:08AM EDT until June 25 at 11:00PM EDT by NWS Indianapolis IN",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Indiana...\nIllinois...\n\nWhite River at Hazleton.\n\nWhite River at Petersburg.\n\nWabash River at Riverton.\n\nWabash River at Hutsonville Legacy Power Plant Site.\n\n...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in\nIllinois...Indiana...\n\nWabash River at Mount Carmel.\n\nWabash River at Vincennes.\n\n.Minor flooding continues on the White River from Petersburg\ndown to the Wabash...and on the Wabash River from the Hutsonville\narea down to Mount Carmel. The crest on the White was near Hazleton\nwhile the crest on the Wabash was near Vincennes late Wednesday\nmorning.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Wabash River at Vincennes.\n\n* WHEN...Until late tomorrow evening.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 17.0 feet, Considerable agricultural flooding extends\nfrom just north of the junction of Illinois 33 with Business 50 to\nthe St. Francesville, Illinois area.  River Road from Lincoln\nMemorial Bridge to Billett Rd is impassable.  Extensive seep water\nforms behind Illinois levees extending from Russellville to U.S.\nHighway 50.  Flooding of agricultural land begins in Knox County\nIndiana west of the railroad extending for the Oaktown area to the\nnorth side of Vincennes.  Extensive flooding of Small Creek.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 10:45 AM EDT Wednesday /9:45 AM CDT Wednesday/ the stage\nwas 16.8 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours\nending at 10:45 AM EDT Wednesday /9:45 AM CDT Wednesday/ was\n16.8 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage\nlate tomorrow morning and continue falling and remain below\nflood stage.\n- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov/ind.\n\nThe next statement should be issued this evening by around 1100 PM\nEDT /1000 PM CDT/.",

            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 10:08AM CDT until June 29 at 1:00AM CDT by NWS Mobile AL",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning is extended for the following river in\nMississippi...\n\nPascagoula At Merrill affecting George, Greene and Jackson\nCounties.\n\nFor the Pascagoula River...including Merrill...Minor flooding is\nforecast.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov/mob. Click on\nthe Rivers and Lakes menu for forecasts and observations.\n\nThe next statement will be issued when updates occur.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Pascagoula at Merrill.\n\n* WHEN...Until late Sunday night.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 23.5 feet, water is under homes in Plum Bluff Estates.\nStreets of Merrill flood. At 24.0 feet, streets of Merrill will\nbecome flooded. At 24 feet the bridge becomes inaccessible by\nvehicles.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 9:15 AM CDT Wednesday the stage was 24.2 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending\nat 9:15 AM CDT Wednesday was 24.3 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 24.2 feet\nthis afternoon.             "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 10:05AM CDT by NWS Mobile AL",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following river in\nMississippi...\n\nChickasawhay At Leakesville affecting George and Greene Counties.\n\nFor the Chickasawhay River...including Waynesboro, Leakesville...\nMinor flooding is forecast.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov/mob. Click on\nthe Rivers and Lakes menu for forecasts and observations.\n\nThe next statement will be issued when updates occur.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Chickasawhay at Leakesville.\n\n* WHEN...Until further notice.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 26.0 feet, flooding at the highway bridge begins.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 9:15 AM CDT Wednesday the stage was 26.4 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending\nat 9:15 AM CDT Wednesday was 26.4 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to fall to 23.9 feet Monday\nmorning.\n- Flood stage is 20.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",

            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following river in Florida...\nAlabama...\n\nEscambia River Near Century affecting Escambia and Santa Rosa\nCounties.\n\nFor the Escambia River...including Century...Minor flooding is\nforecast.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov/mob. At 19.0 feet, low lying pastures will flood.             "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 9:43AM CDT by NWS St Louis MO",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nIllinois...\n\nIllinois River at Meredosia.\n\nIllinois River at La Grange LD.\n\nIllinois River at Valley City.\n\nIllinois River at Hardin.\n\nRiver forecasts are based on observed precipitation and forecast\nprecipitation for the next 24 hours.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Illinois River at Valley City.\n\n* WHEN...Until further notice.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 9:30 AM CDT Wednesday the stage was 17.0 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending\nat 9:30 AM CDT Wednesday was 17.0 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 17.6 feet\nearly Sunday morning.\n- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.",
            "instruction": "Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars\nthrough flooded areas.\n\nThis product, along with additional weather and stream information,\nis available at https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/lsx",

            "event": "Flood Warning",
            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS St Louis MO",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 9:43AM CDT by NWS St Louis MO",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nIllinois...\n\nIllinois River at Meredosia.\n\nIllinois River at La Grange LD.\n\nIllinois River at Valley City.\n\nIllinois River at Hardin.\n\nRiver forecasts are based on observed precipitation and forecast\nprecipitation for the next 24 hours.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Illinois River at La Grange LD.\n\n* WHEN...Until further notice.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 9:00 AM CDT Wednesday the stage was 25.6 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending\nat 9:00 AM CDT Wednesday was 25.6 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 26.0 feet\nFriday evening.\n- Flood stage is 23.0 feet.",
            "instruction": "Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars\nthrough flooded areas.\n\nThis product, along with additional weather and stream information,\nis available at https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/lsx",
            "response": "Avoid",
            "note": null,
            "parameters": {

            "senderName": "NWS Lincoln IL",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 9:39AM CDT until June 28 at 3:24PM CDT by NWS Lincoln IL",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in\nIllinois...\n\nEmbarras River at Lawrenceville affecting Lawrence County.\n\n.The following forecasts are based on observed precipitation, soil\nmoisture conditions, and forecast precipitation.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Embarras River at Lawrenceville.\n\n* WHEN...Until Sunday afternoon.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 33.0 feet, Kelly's Lake Lane, 1160N, is inundated.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 8:45 AM CDT Wednesday the stage was 32.0 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours\nending at 8:45 AM CDT Wednesday was 32.0 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 32.1\nfeet this evening. It will then fall below flood stage late\nSunday morning.\n- Flood stage is 30.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Persons with interests along this river need to remain aware of the\nlatest forecasts and associated flood risk for their area. Stay\ntuned for further updates on this flooding situation.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.",
            "response": "Avoid",
            "note": null,

            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 9:29AM CDT by NWS Shreveport LA",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nArkansas...Louisiana...\n\nBayou Dorcheat Near Springhill affecting Columbia and Webster\nParishes.\n\nFor the Bayou Dorcheat...including Springhill...Minor flooding is\nforecast.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Bayou Dorcheat near Springhill.\n\n* WHEN...Until further notice.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 13.0 feet, Minor lowland flooding of private boat\nramps. Move livestock to higher ground.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 9:00 AM CDT Wednesday the stage was 12.8 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 13.5 feet\nearly Friday afternoon.\n- Flood stage is 11.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Do not drive cars through flooded areas. Caution is urged when\nwalking near riverbanks. Turn around, don't drown when encountering\nflooded roads.             "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 9:27AM CDT until June 27 at 10:00AM CDT by NWS Shreveport LA",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...\n\nSulphur River Near Talco affecting Titus, Bowie, Franklin, Morris\nand Red River Counties.\n\nFor the Sulphur River...including Talco...Minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Sulphur River near Talco.\n\n* WHEN...Until Saturday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 20.0 feet, Expect minor lowland flooding of the\nheavily wooded floodplain. Ranchers that may have cattle and\nequipment in the river bottoms should move them to higher ground.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 8:45 AM CDT Wednesday the stage was 20.6 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending\nat 8:45 AM CDT Wednesday was 20.6 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 22.0 feet\njust after midnight tonight. It will then fall below flood stage\nFriday afternoon.\n- Flood stage is 20.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Do not drive cars through flooded areas. Caution is urged when\nwalking near riverbanks. Turn around, don't drown when encountering\nflooded roads.             "senderName": "NWS Lincoln IL",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 9:07AM CDT by NWS Lincoln IL",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in\nIllinois...\n\nLittle Wabash River below Clay City affecting Richland and Clay\nCounties.\n\n.The following forecasts are based on observed precipitation, soil\nmoisture conditions, and forecast precipitation.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Little Wabash River below Clay City.\n\n* WHEN...Until further notice.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 22.0 feet, North Clay Road...1 mile east of the gage\nis flooded.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 8:45 AM CDT Wednesday the stage was 21.0 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours\nending at 8:45 AM CDT Wednesday was 21.0 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to fall to 19.4 feet Monday\nmorning.\n- Flood stage is 18.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Persons with interests along this river need to remain aware of the\nlatest forecasts and associated flood risk for their area. Stay\ntuned for further updates on this flooding situation.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.",
            "response": "Avoid",
            "note": null,

            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 9:04AM CDT until June 28 at 1:36AM CDT by NWS Jackson MS",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nMississippi...\n\nBig Black River Near Bentonia affecting Madison and Yazoo\nCounties.\n\nBig Black River Near Bovina affecting Warren and Hinds Counties.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Big Black River near Bovina.\n\n* WHEN...Until early Sunday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 32.0 feet, Several access roads along and near the\nriver are under water.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 8:15 AM CDT Wednesday the stage was 27.4 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage\nearly tomorrow afternoon to a crest of 31.0 feet Friday\nmorning.\n- Flood stage is 28.0 feet.\n- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of\n31.0 feet on 09/27/2002.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive\ncars through flooded areas.\n\nTurn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.water.noaa.gov/wfo/jan\n\nThe next statement will be issued this evening at 915 PM CDT.",

            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 8:52AM CDT until June 27 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS Chicago IL",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in\nIllinois...\n\nIllinois River at La Salle affecting Putnam, Bureau and La Salle\nCounties.\n\nFor the Illinois River (Upper)...including La Salle...Minor flooding\nis forecast.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Illinois River from Starved Rock Lock and Dam downstream\nto confluence with Big Bureau Creek, including the La Salle gauge.\n\n* WHEN...Until Saturday evening.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 22.0 feet, Lower parking lot at Starved Rock State\nPark is inundated east of La Salle. High water levels begin to\nimpact shipping interests along the river.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:45 AM CDT Wednesday the stage was 22.8 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage\nSaturday afternoon.\n- Flood stage is 20.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "A Flood Warning means water levels above flood stage are imminent or\nmay already be occurring. Persons along rivers and streams in the\nwarned area should take immediate precautions to protect life and\nproperty.\n\nThese forecasts are based on observed precipitation as well as\nforecast precipitation 24 hours into the future. Changes to the\nrainfall forecast, or any additional rainfall after 24 hours, may\ncause changes to these river forecasts.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.\n\nThe next statement will be issued by late tonight.",

            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 8:46AM CDT by NWS Lincoln IL",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in\nIllinois...\n\nIllinois River at Henry affecting Putnam and Marshall Counties.\n\n...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nIllinois...\n\nIllinois River at Peoria affecting Woodford, Peoria and Tazewell\nCounties.\n\nIllinois River at Beardstown affecting Schuyler, Brown, Morgan\nand Cass Counties.\n\nIllinois River near Havana affecting Fulton, Cass and Mason\nCounties.\n\n.The following forecasts are based on observed precipitation, soil\nmoisture conditions, and forecast precipitation.\n\n* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is\nforecast.\n\n* WHERE...Illinois River at Beardstown.\n\n* WHEN...Until further notice.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 20.0 feet, Seepage problems begin in the South\nBeardstown Drainage and Levee District.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:45 AM CDT Wednesday the stage was 20.7 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours\nending at 7:45 AM CDT Wednesday was 20.7 feet.\n- Forecast...The river will rise to 21.1 feet early Sunday\nmorning. It will then fall Sunday morning. It will rise to\n21.1 feet early Monday morning. It will then fall again but\nremain above flood stage.\n- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Persons with interests along this river need to remain aware of the\nlatest forecasts and associated flood risk for their area. Stay\ntuned for further updates on this flooding situation.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.",

            "description": "...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in\nIllinois...\n\nIllinois River at Henry affecting Putnam and Marshall Counties.\n\n...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nIllinois...\n\nIllinois River at Peoria affecting Woodford, Peoria and Tazewell\nCounties.\n\nIllinois River at Beardstown affecting Schuyler, Brown, Morgan\nand Cass Counties.\n\nIllinois River near Havana affecting Fulton, Cass and Mason\nCounties.\n\n.The following forecasts are based on observed precipitation, soil\nmoisture conditions, and forecast precipitation.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Illinois River at Peoria.\n\n* WHEN...Until further notice.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 22.7 feet, Flooding begins to low lying areas in\nPeoria Heights and Peoria's Riverfront Park.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:45 AM CDT Wednesday the stage was 20.5 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours\nending at 7:45 AM CDT Wednesday was 20.5 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 20.9\nfeet tomorrow morning.\n- Flood stage is 18.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Persons with interests along this river need to remain aware of the\nlatest forecasts and associated flood risk for their area. Stay\ntuned for further updates on this flooding situation.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.",

            "event": "Flood Warning",
            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Lincoln IL",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 8:46AM CDT until June 29 at 1:00AM CDT by NWS Lincoln IL",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in\nIllinois...\n\nIllinois River at Henry affecting Putnam and Marshall Counties.\n\n...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nIllinois...\n\nIllinois River at Peoria affecting Woodford, Peoria and Tazewell\nCounties.\n\nIllinois River at Beardstown affecting Schuyler, Brown, Morgan\nand Cass Counties.\n\nIllinois River near Havana affecting Fulton, Cass and Mason\nCounties.\n\n.The following forecasts are based on observed precipitation, soil\nmoisture conditions, and forecast precipitation.\n\n* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is\nforecast.\n\n* WHERE...Illinois River at Henry.\n\n* WHEN...Until early Monday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 23.0 feet, Water begins to affect the marina in Henry\nalong with minor flooding of land adjacent to the river.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:45 AM CDT Wednesday the stage was 24.2 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours\nending at 7:45 AM CDT Wednesday was 24.2 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 24.4\nfeet just after midnight tonight. It will then fall below\nflood stage Sunday evening.\n- Flood stage is 23.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Persons with interests along this river need to remain aware of the\nlatest forecasts and associated flood risk for their area. Stay\ntuned for further updates on this flooding situation.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.",
            "response": "Avoid",
            "note": null,

            "description": "...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in\nIllinois...\n\nIllinois River at Henry affecting Putnam and Marshall Counties.\n\n...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nIllinois...\n\nIllinois River at Peoria affecting Woodford, Peoria and Tazewell\nCounties.\n\nIllinois River at Beardstown affecting Schuyler, Brown, Morgan\nand Cass Counties.\n\nIllinois River near Havana affecting Fulton, Cass and Mason\nCounties.\n\n.The following forecasts are based on observed precipitation, soil\nmoisture conditions, and forecast precipitation.\n\n* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is\nforecast.\n\n* WHERE...Illinois River near Havana.\n\n* WHEN...Until further notice.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 19.5 feet, Access road to Anderson Lake north\ncampground closed.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:45 AM CDT Wednesday the stage was 19.5 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours\nending at 7:45 AM CDT Wednesday was 19.5 feet.\n- Forecast...The river will rise to 19.8 feet Friday morning.\nIt will then fall Sunday evening. It will rise to 19.6 feet\nearly Monday morning. It will then fall again but remain\nabove flood stage.\n- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",

            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nMississippi...\n\nPascagoula River At Graham Ferry affecting Jackson County.\n\nFor the Pascagoula River...including Graham Ferry...Minor flooding is\nforecast.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Pascagoula River at Graham Ferry.\n\n* WHEN...Until further notice.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 16.0 feet, River property at Cumbest Bluff will be cut\noff by high water and some river roads will be impassable.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:45 AM CDT Wednesday the stage was 16.9 feet.\n- Bankfull stage is 15.0 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending\nat 7:45 AM CDT Wednesday was 17.0 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 17.5 feet\nearly Friday morning.\n- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.\n- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 17.5\nfeet on 09/05/2012.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nMotorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars\nthrough flooded areas.\n\nPlease report observed flooding to local emergency services or law\nenforcement and request they pass this information to the National\nWeather Service when you can do so safely.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov/lix.  Click on\nthe Rivers and Lakes menu for forecasts and observations.\n\nThe next statement will be issued when updates are needed.",
            "response": "Avoid",
            "note": null,
            "parameters": {

              ],

            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Houston/Galveston TX",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 8:32AM CDT until June 26 at 1:00AM CDT by NWS Houston/Galveston TX",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...\n\nNavasota River near Normangee affecting Grimes, Brazos and\nMadison Counties.\n\nFor the Navasota River...including Normangee...Minor flooding is\nforecast.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Navasota River near Normangee.\n\n* WHEN...Until early Friday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 15.0 feet, Minor lowland flooding begins as water\nescapes the main channel and inundates the floodplain.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:00 AM CDT Wednesday the stage was 15.9 feet.\n- Bankfull stage is 12.0 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours\nending at 7:00 AM CDT Wednesday was 17.3 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage\nearly tomorrow afternoon and continue falling to 7.9 feet\nMonday morning.\n- Flood stage is 15.0 feet.\n- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of\n15.9 feet on 02/02/2010.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nMotorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive\ncars through flooded areas.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov/hgx.\n\nThe next statement will be issued by late tonight at 245 AM CDT.",
            "response": "Avoid",
            "note": null,

              ],

            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Tallahassee FL",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 9:09AM EDT until June 29 at 2:00AM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in\nFlorida...\n\nChoctawhatchee River near Bruce (SR 20) affecting Washington and\nWalton Counties.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Choctawhatchee River near Bruce (SR 20).\n\n* WHEN...From this morning to early Monday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 14.0 feet, Big Cedar, Cowford, and Choctawhatchee\nRiver Roads begin to flood in Walton County. Flood waters impact\nstorage areas underneath homes on the west banks of the\nChoctawhatchee River. Low areas along Strickland Road in\nWashington County become subject to flooding.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 8 AM CDT Wednesday the stage was estimated to be around\n14.0 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage\nlate this morning to a crest of 14.8 feet early tomorrow\nafternoon. It will then fall below flood stage Sunday\nmorning.\n- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.\n- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of\n14.8 feet on 03/11/1934.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.\n\nTurn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.\n\nThe next statement will be issued this evening at 1000 PM CDT.",
            "response": "Avoid",

            "senderName": "NWS Shreveport LA",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 7:59AM CDT until June 28 at 1:00AM CDT by NWS Shreveport LA",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...\n\nAngelina River Near Angelina River at Hwy 59 near Lufkin affecting\nAngelina and Nacogdoches Counties.\n\nFor the Angelina River...including Angelina River at Hwy 59 near\nLufkin...Minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Angelina River near Angelina River at Hwy 59 near Lufkin.\n\n* WHEN...Until late Saturday night.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 161.0 feet, Expect minor flooding with the gravel\nparking lot flooded and water beginning to overflow the gravel road\nwhere it widens into the parking lot.  Also expect about a foot of\noverflow across the left bank of the Angelina River looking\ndownstream.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:45 AM CDT Wednesday the stage was 161.1 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending\nat 7:45 AM CDT Wednesday was 161.7 feet.\n- Forecast...The river will remain on a slow fall and then fall\nbelow flood stage early Friday afternoon.\n- Flood stage is 161.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Do not drive cars through flooded areas. Caution is urged when\nwalking near riverbanks. Turn around, don't drown when encountering\nflooded roads. Most flood deaths occur in vehicles.\n\nFor more hydrologic information, copy and paste the following website\naddress into your favorite web browser URL bar:\nhttps://water.noaa.gov/wfo/SHV\n\nThe next statement will be issued Thursday morning at 800 AM CDT.",

            "description": "...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...\n\nNeches River Near Diboll affecting Angelina, Trinity and Polk\nCounties.\n\nFor the Neches River...including Diboll...Minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Neches River near Diboll.\n\n* WHEN...From Friday afternoon to late Saturday night.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 12.0 feet, Minor lowland flooding occurs.             "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Shreveport LA",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 7:56AM CDT by NWS Shreveport LA",
            "description": "...The National Weather Service in Shreveport has issued a Flood\nWarning for the following rivers in Louisiana...\n\nBayou D'Arbonne At Lake D'Arbonne affecting Union Parish.\n\nFor the Bayou D'arbonne...including Lake D'Arbonne...Minor flooding\nis forecast.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Bayou D'Arbonne at Lake D'Arbonne.\n\n* WHEN...From Thursday afternoon until further notice.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 83.0 feet, Expect flooding of secondary roadways with\nsome camps suffering overflow. Boats should be moved from\nboathouses to prevent damage to boats and boathouses, otherwise\nboats may actually rise through the roofs of boathouses with the\nhigh water. At 84.0 feet, Expect significant flooding of several\nsecondary roadways that will result in several residents being\ncutoff from major highways. Several homes in low areas will be in\ndanger of flooding and homeowners should take steps to protect\nproperty. Nearly all camps will suffer from flooding.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 6:45 AM CDT Wednesday the stage was 81.3 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage\ntomorrow afternoon and continue rising to a crest of 84.0 feet\nearly Saturday morning.\n- Flood stage is 83.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Do not drive cars through flooded areas. Caution is urged when\nwalking near riverbanks. Turn around, don't drown when encountering\nflooded roads. Most flood deaths occur in vehicles.\n\nFor more hydrologic information, copy and paste the following website\naddress into your favorite web browser URL bar:\nhttps://water.noaa.gov/wfo/SHV\n\nThe next statement will be issued Thursday morning at 800 AM CDT.",
            "response": "Avoid",
            "note": null,

            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 8:37AM EDT by NWS Jacksonville FL",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Georgia...\n\nSatilla River At Waycross affecting Ware and Pierce Counties.\n\nSatilla River At Atkinson affecting Brantley County.\n\nAdditional information is available at\nhttps://water.weather.gov/wfo/JAX\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Satilla River at Atkinson.\n\n* WHEN...Until further notice.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 13.0 feet, Warners Landing, Louis Landing and\nsecondary roads around KOA campgrounds begin to flood.\nAt 14.0 feet, River Rock Road begins to experience flooding across\nthe road.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:45 AM EDT Wednesday the stage was 12.7 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage\nthis afternoon and continue rising to 16.3 feet Saturday\nmorning. Additional rises are possible thereafter.\n- Flood stage is 13.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",

            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 8:37AM EDT until June 26 at 10:01PM EDT by NWS Jacksonville FL",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Georgia...\n\nSatilla River At Waycross affecting Ware and Pierce Counties.\n\nSatilla River At Atkinson affecting Brantley County.\n\nAdditional information is available at\nhttps://water.weather.gov/wfo/JAX\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Satilla River at Waycross.\n\n* WHEN...Until late Friday evening.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 16.0 feet, Flooding of agriculture and timberlands\nbegins. On the Ware County side, the Jamestown Road Boat Ramp is\nflooded. On the Pierce/Brantley county line at the State Road 121\nBridge the boat ramp and dirt access roads are flooded.\nAt 17.0 feet, On the Ware County side, the Jamestown Road Boat\nRamp parking lot and access road is flooded and Simmons Trail is\nflooded cutting off one residence. On the Pierce County side, the\nOkefenokee Country Club Course Holes 14 through 16 begin to flood.\nAt 18.0 feet, On the Pierce County side, the Okefenokee Country\nClub Golf Course is generally closed. Riverwoods Drive low lying\nproperties begin to flood.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 8:30 AM EDT Wednesday the stage was 17.0 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 17.2\nfeet this evening. It will then fall below flood stage Friday\nafternoon.\n- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",

            "senderName": "NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM",
            "headline": "Heat Advisory issued June 24 at 5:54AM MDT until June 25 at 9:00PM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM",
            "description": "* WHAT...Highs of 104 to 108.\n\n* WHERE...In New Mexico, Southern Dona Ana County/Mesilla Valley. In\nTexas, Eastern/Central El Paso County, Rio Grande Valley of\nEastern El Paso/Western Hudspeth Counties, Rio Grande Valley of\nEastern Hudspeth County, and Western El Paso County.\n\n* WHEN...Until 9 PM MDT Thursday.\n\n* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures may cause heat illnesses.",
            "instruction": "Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose\nfitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning\nor evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and\nheat stroke.\n\nTo reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and\nHealth Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in\nshaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat\nshould be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an\nemergency! Call 9 1 1.\n\nDrink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of\nthe sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.",
            "response": "Execute",
            "note": null,

            "senderName": "NWS Flagstaff AZ",
            "headline": "Fire Weather Watch issued June 24 at 12:12AM MST until June 28 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ",
            "description": "* WHAT...Critical fire weather conditions. Southwest winds 20 to 30\nmph with gusts 40 to 50 mph and relative humidity 8 to 16 percent\nexpected each afternoon.\n\n* WHERE...All of northern Arizona.\n\n* WHEN...From Friday morning through Sunday evening.\n\n* IMPACTS...Rapid spread and growth of any new or existing fires.\nFires will have the potential to exhibit extreme fire behavior.\nElevated potential for new fire starts. Winds may damage power\nlines, resulting in new fire starts.",
            "instruction": "A Fire Weather Watch means that critical fire weather conditions are\npossible. These conditions could promote the rapid spread and growth\nof wildfires, which could become life-threatening. For forecast\nupdates, go to weather.gov/flagstaff.\n\nIf you have not packed your go kit yet, now is the time to do so.\nThis includes items like important documents and essentials you\ncannot live without. Fill your vehicle's fuel tank. Visit\nready.gov/kit for more information.\n\nObey all fire restrictions. To view a map of current fire\nrestrictions, go to wildlandfire.az.gov/fire-restrictions.\n\nPlease advise the appropriate officials or fire crews in the field of\nthis Fire Weather Watch.",
            "response": "Prepare",

            "headline": "Heat Advisory issued June 24 at 12:02AM MDT until June 24 at 8:00PM MDT by NWS Midland/Odessa TX",
            "description": "* WHAT...Temperatures up to 99 degrees in the mountains, up to 109 in\nthe adjacent plains, and up to 114 in the Rio Grande Valley.\n\n* WHERE...Portions of southeast New Mexico and southwest and western\nTexas.\n\n* WHEN...From 1 PM MDT /2 PM CDT/ to 8 PM MDT /9 PM CDT/ Wednesday.\n\n* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures may cause heat illnesses. Extreme heat\nwill significantly increase the potential for heat related\nillnesses, particularly for those working or participating in\noutdoor activities.",
            "instruction": "Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose\nfitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning\nor evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and\nheat stroke.\n\nTo reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and\nHealth Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in\nshaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat\nshould be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an\nemergency! Call 9 1 1.\n\nLook before you lock! Do not leave young children and pets in\nunattended vehicles for even a moment. Car interiors will very\nquickly reach lethal temperatures.",
            "response": "Execute",
            "note": null,
